Then he said: We do not know it to be narrated except through this route. [[Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/473) through Hisham ibn 'Ammar and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid, both from al-Walid ibn Muslim.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

He, the Exalted, informs of His grace and mercy toward His creation: that He sent down the Qur'an to His servants and made its memorisation and understanding easy for whomever He has mercy upon. He said: ﴿The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an. Created man. Taught him eloquence.﴾ Al-Hasan said: it means speech (al-nutq). Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said: it means good and evil. Al-Hasan's view here is better and stronger, because the context concerns His teaching of the Qur'an, which is the performance of its recitation, and this is only through making speech easy for the creation and facilitating the exit of the letters from their points of articulation in the throat, tongue and lips, according to the variety of their places of articulation and types.

* *

His saying: ﴿The sun and the moon [move] by calculation﴾, meaning: they run successively by a precisely measured reckoning, which does not vary or fluctuate, ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each [celestial body] is swimming in an orbit﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He splits the dawn and made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Al-An'am: 96].

It is related from 'Ikrimah that he said: If Allah placed the light of the sight of all humans, jinn, animals and birds into the eyes of one servant, then removed a single veil out of seventy veils between him and the sun, he would not be able to look at it. The light of the sun is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Kursi, the light of the Kursi is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Throne, and the light of the Throne is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Veil. So consider what Allah gives His servant of light in his eyes at the time of looking upon the face of his Generous Lord directly. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾. Ibn Jarir said: The commentators differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿and the star﴾, though they agreed that the tree (shajar) is that which stands upon a stalk. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The najm is that which spreads out upon the face of the earth," meaning of plants. Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi and Sufyan al-Thawri. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose this view.

Mujahid said: an-najm is that which is in the sky. Likewise said al-Hasan and Qatadah. This view is the most apparent, and Allah knows best, due to His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the animals, and many among mankind?﴾ [Al-Hajj: 18], and the verse continues.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the sky He raised and set the balance﴾, meaning: justice, as He said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Book and the balance that people may maintain justice﴾ [Al-Hadid: 25]. Likewise He said here: ﴿that you not transgress in the balance﴾, meaning: He created the heavens and the earth with truth and justice, so that all things would be with truth and justice. Therefore He said: ﴿And establish weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance﴾, meaning: do not diminish the weight, but weigh with truth and fairness, as He said [the Exalted]: ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 182].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures﴾, meaning: just as He raised the sky, He laid down the earth and spread it out, and anchored it with firm, towering mountains, so that it would be stable for what is upon its surface of the creatures (al-anam), who are the diverse creations of differing types, forms, colours and languages, in all its regions and corners. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: al-anam means the creation.

﴿Therein is fruit﴾, meaning: of varying colours, tastes and aromas. ﴿And the palm with its sheathed clusters﴾: He singled it out for mention because of its nobility and benefit, fresh and dry. Al-akmam: Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn 'Abbas: they are the sheaths of the spathe (al-tal'). So said more than one of the commentators: it is that from which the spathe emerges, then splits to reveal the cluster, becoming unripe dates (busr), then ripe dates (rutab), then it matures and its ripeness and full development are complete.

Ibn Abi Hatim said, related from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Sayrafi: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, Yunus ibn al-Harith al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Caesar wrote to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "I inform you that my messengers came to me from your side, and claimed that among you there is a tree that is not good for anything of goodness; it emerges like the ears of donkeys, then splits like pearls, then turns green and becomes like green emerald, then reddens and becomes like red ruby, then ripens and matures and becomes like the finest pastry eaten, then dries and becomes a protection for the resident and provision for the traveller. If my messengers have told me the truth, I see this tree as nothing other than a tree of Paradise." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote back to him: "From 'Umar, Commander of the Believers, to Caesar, king of the Romans: Your messengers have told you the truth. This tree is with us, and it is the tree that Allah caused to grow for Mary when she gave birth to Jesus her son. So fear Allah and do not take Jesus as a god besides Allah, for ﴿the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was. It is also said: al-akmam are its ruf'at (rufat), which is the fibre that is on the neck of the palm tree. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

﴿And the grain having husk and the fragrant plant﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿the grain having husk﴾ means the chaff (tibn).

'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-asf is the leaves of the green crop whose heads have been cut; when it dries it is called al-asf. Likewise said Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Abu Malik: its asf is its chaff.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾ means the leaves.

Al-Hasan said: it is your fragrant plant (rayhan) this one.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾ means the greenness of the crop.

The meaning of this, and Allah knows best, is that grain such as wheat, barley and the like has, in the state of its growth, asf, which is what is on the ear, and rayhan, which is the leaves wrapped around its stalk.

It is also said: al-asf is the leaves when the crop first sprouts as herbage, and al-rayhan is the leaves when it has ripened and the grain has formed within it, as Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl said in his famous qasidah:

"Say to Him: who causes the grain to grow in the earth, so that from it the herbage becomes swaying and high? And brings forth its grain in its heads? In that are signs for whoever is attentive."

* *

His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾, meaning: So which of the favours of Allah, O assembly of the two weighty groups, of mankind and jinn, would you deny? Said Mujahid and more than one. The context after it indicates this: the blessings are manifest upon you, and you are immersed in them, unable to deny them or reject them. So we say, as the believing jinn said: "O Allah, none of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny; to You belongs all praise." His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾, meaning: So which of the favours of Allah, O assembly of the two weighty groups, of mankind and jinn, would you deny? Said Mujahid and more than one. The context after it indicates this: the blessings are manifest upon you, and you are immersed in them, unable to deny them or reject them. So we say, as the believing jinn said: "O Allah, none of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny; to You belongs all praise." Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "None of them, O Lord," meaning: we do not deny any of them.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting while praying facing the Corner, before he was commanded to declare openly, and the polytheists were listening: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [[Al-Musnad (6/349).]]

Tafsir of Surah Ar-Rahman

It is a Meccan surah.

Imam Ahmad said: Affan narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Zirr, that a man said to Ibn Mas'ud: "How do you read this letter: 'ma'in ghayri yasin aw asin' (water unchanged or stagnant)?" He said: "Have you read the whole Qur'an?" He said: "I read the mufassal (the later short surahs) all together in one rak'ah." He said: "Racing through it like the rushing of poetry, may you have no father? I know the pairs (qara'in) of the Prophet ﷺ, which he would recite two by two from the beginning of the mufassal, and the first of Ibn Mas'ud's mufassal was: ﴿The Most Merciful﴾ [Ar-Rahman]." [[Al-Musnad (1/412).]]

Abu 'Isa at-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid Abu Muslim narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to his Companions and recited to them the surah "Ar-Rahman" from its beginning to its end. They remained silent, so he said: "I recited it to the jinn on the night of the jinn, and they were better in their response than you. Every time I reached His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ they said: 'None of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny; to You belongs all praise.'" [[Sunan at-Tirmidhi, no. 3291.]]

Then he said: This is a strange (gharib) hadith; we do not know it except through the hadith of al-Walid ibn Muslim from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad. Then he related from Imam Ahmad that he did not recognise it and disapproved of the narration of the people of Syria from this Zuhayr ibn Muhammad.

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar also narrated it from 'Amr ibn Malik, from al-Walid ibn Muslim; and from 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabbawayh, from Hisham ibn 'Ammar, both of them from al-Walid ibn Muslim, with the same chain. Then he said: We do not know it to be narrated except through this route. [[Al-Hakim also narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/473) through Hisham ibn 'Ammar and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Waqid, both from al-Walid ibn Muslim.]]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Musa and 'Amr ibn Malik al-Basri narrated to us, both saying: Yahya ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Umayyah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited the surah "Ar-Rahman" (or it was recited in his presence), and said: "What is the matter with me that I hear the jinn giving a better answer to their Lord than you?" They said: "And what is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Whenever I reached the saying of Allah: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾, the jinn said: 'None of the blessings of our Lord do we deny.'"

Al-Hafiz al-Bazzar narrated it from 'Amr ibn Malik with the same chain. [[Musnad al-Bazzar (2269), Kashf al-Astar; his shaykh 'Amr ibn Malik al-Rasibi was declared weak by the majority, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy.]] Then he said: We do not know it to be narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this route with this chain.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

He, the Exalted, informs of His grace and mercy toward His creation: that He sent down the Qur'an to His servants and made its memorisation and understanding easy for whomever He has mercy upon. He said: ﴿The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an. Created man. Taught him eloquence.﴾ Al-Hasan said: it means speech (al-nutq). Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others said: it means good and evil. Al-Hasan's view here is better and stronger, because the context concerns His teaching of the Qur'an, which is the performance of its recitation, and this is only through making speech easy for the creation and facilitating the exit of the letters from their points of articulation in the throat, tongue and lips, according to the variety of their places of articulation and types.

* *

His saying: ﴿The sun and the moon [move] by calculation﴾, meaning: they run successively by a precisely measured reckoning, which does not vary or fluctuate, ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day; each [celestial body] is swimming in an orbit﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He splits the dawn and made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Al-An'am: 96].

It is related from 'Ikrimah that he said: If Allah placed the light of the sight of all humans, jinn, animals and birds into the eyes of one servant, then removed a single veil out of seventy veils between him and the sun, he would not be able to look at it. The light of the sun is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Kursi, the light of the Kursi is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Throne, and the light of the Throne is one part of seventy parts of the light of the Veil. So consider what Allah gives His servant of light in his eyes at the time of looking upon the face of his Generous Lord directly. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾. Ibn Jarir said: The commentators differed concerning the meaning of His saying ﴿and the star﴾, though they agreed that the tree (shajar) is that which stands upon a stalk. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The najm is that which spreads out upon the face of the earth," meaning of plants. Likewise said Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi and Sufyan al-Thawri. Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on him, chose this view.

Mujahid said: an-najm is that which is in the sky. Likewise said al-Hasan and Qatadah. This view is the most apparent, and Allah knows best, due to His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the animals, and many among mankind?﴾ [Al-Hajj: 18], and the verse continues.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the sky He raised and set the balance﴾, meaning: justice, as He said: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear evidences and sent down with them the Book and the balance that people may maintain justice﴾ [Al-Hadid: 25]. Likewise He said here: ﴿that you not transgress in the balance﴾, meaning: He created the heavens and the earth with truth and justice, so that all things would be with truth and justice. Therefore He said: ﴿And establish weight with justice and do not make deficient the balance﴾, meaning: do not diminish the weight, but weigh with truth and fairness, as He said [the Exalted]: ﴿And weigh with an even balance﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 182].

* *

His saying: ﴿And the earth He laid out for the creatures﴾, meaning: just as He raised the sky, He laid down the earth and spread it out, and anchored it with firm, towering mountains, so that it would be stable for what is upon its surface of the creatures (al-anam), who are the diverse creations of differing types, forms, colours and languages, in all its regions and corners. Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: al-anam means the creation.

﴿Therein is fruit﴾, meaning: of varying colours, tastes and aromas. ﴿And the palm with its sheathed clusters﴾: He singled it out for mention because of its nobility and benefit, fresh and dry. Al-akmam: Ibn Jurayj said, from Ibn 'Abbas: they are the sheaths of the spathe (al-tal'). So said more than one of the commentators: it is that from which the spathe emerges, then splits to reveal the cluster, becoming unripe dates (busr), then ripe dates (rutab), then it matures and its ripeness and full development are complete.

Ibn Abi Hatim said, related from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Sayrafi: Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, Yunus ibn al-Harith al-Ta'ifi narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Caesar wrote to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: "I inform you that my messengers came to me from your side, and claimed that among you there is a tree that is not good for anything of goodness; it emerges like the ears of donkeys, then splits like pearls, then turns green and becomes like green emerald, then reddens and becomes like red ruby, then ripens and matures and becomes like the finest pastry eaten, then dries and becomes a protection for the resident and provision for the traveller. If my messengers have told me the truth, I see this tree as nothing other than a tree of Paradise." 'Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote back to him: "From 'Umar, Commander of the Believers, to Caesar, king of the Romans: Your messengers have told you the truth. This tree is with us, and it is the tree that Allah caused to grow for Mary when she gave birth to Jesus her son. So fear Allah and do not take Jesus as a god besides Allah, for ﴿the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like that of Adam; He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59-60]."

It is also said: al-akmam are its ruf'at (rufat), which is the fibre that is on the neck of the palm tree. This is the view of al-Hasan and Qatadah.

﴿And the grain having husk and the fragrant plant﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿the grain having husk﴾ means the chaff (tibn).

'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: al-asf is the leaves of the green crop whose heads have been cut; when it dries it is called al-asf. Likewise said Qatadah, al-Dahhak and Abu Malik: its asf is its chaff.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾ means the leaves.

Al-Hasan said: it is your fragrant plant (rayhan) this one.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and the fragrant plant﴾ means the greenness of the crop.

The meaning of this, and Allah knows best, is that grain such as wheat, barley and the like has, in the state of its growth, asf, which is what is on the ear, and rayhan, which is the leaves wrapped around its stalk.

It is also said: al-asf is the leaves when the crop first sprouts as herbage, and al-rayhan is the leaves when it has ripened and the grain has formed within it, as Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl said in his famous qasidah:

"Say to Him: who causes the grain to grow in the earth, so that from it the herbage becomes swaying and high? And brings forth its grain in its heads? In that are signs for whoever is attentive."

* *

His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾, meaning: So which of the favours of Allah, O assembly of the two weighty groups, of mankind and jinn, would you deny? Said Mujahid and more than one. The context after it indicates this: the blessings are manifest upon you, and you are immersed in them, unable to deny them or reject them. So we say, as the believing jinn said: "O Allah, none of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny; to You belongs all praise." Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "None of them, O Lord," meaning: we do not deny any of them.

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Abu al-Aswad, from 'Urwah, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reciting while praying facing the Corner, before he was commanded to declare openly, and the polytheists were listening: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾ [[Al-Musnad (6/349).]]

Ibn Kathir says: Allah mentions His creation of man from clay like pottery (ṣalṣāl kal-fakhkhār), and His creation of the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire (mārij min nār), which is the tip of its flame. This was said by al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās. ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd also said the same.

Al-ʿAwfī related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿from a smokeless flame of fire﴾ that it means from the flame of the fire, from its best part.

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ﴿from a smokeless flame of fire﴾ that it means from the pure fire. ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others also said the same.

Imam Aḥmad said: ʿAbd al-Razzāq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUrwah, from ʿĀ'ishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The angels were created from light, the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Ādam was created from what has been described to you."

Muslim also narrated it, from Muḥammad ibn Rāfiʿ and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, both from ʿAbd al-Razzāq, with the same chain.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾, its explanation has already passed.

﴿Lord of the two easts and Lord of the two wests﴾ means: the eastern rising points of summer and winter, and the western setting points of summer and winter. In another verse He says: ﴿So I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 40]. This is due to the variation of the sun's risings and its movement each day, and its emergence from them toward the people. In another verse He says: ﴿Lord of the East and the West, there is no god but Him, so take Him as a guardian﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 9]. What is meant here is the category of easts and wests. And since in the variation of these easts and wests there are benefits for creation, both jinn and mankind, He said: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He released the two seas, meeting side by side﴾, Ibn ʿAbbās said: that is, He let them go.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿meeting side by side﴾, Ibn Zayd said: that is, He prevented them from meeting, by placing between them the barrier (barzakh), the partition separating them.

What is meant by ﴿the two seas﴾ is the salt and the sweet. The sweet is these rivers flowing among people. We have already discussed this in Sūrat al-Furqān at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who released the two seas, one sweet and palatable, the other salty and bitter, and placed between them a barrier and a complete prohibition﴾ [al-Furqān: 53]. Ibn Jarīr chose here that what is meant by the two seas is the sea of the sky and the sea of the earth, and this is related from Mujāhid, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿAṭiyyah and Ibn Abzā.

Ibn Jarīr said: because pearls are generated from rain water, and from the shells of the sea of the earth. [Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (27/75)]. Although this is so, the meaning is not [by that] what he went to, for the wording does not support it. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿between them is a barrier they do not transgress﴾, that is, He placed between them a barrier, which is a partition of earth, so that one does not transgress against the other, and so that each of them does not corrupt the other and remove it from its characteristic which is intended from it. And what is between the sky and the earth is not called a barzakh or a prohibited partition.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿From them come forth the pearl and the coral﴾, that is: from both of them together; when it is found in one of them, it suffices, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-Anʿām: 130], and the messengers were only among mankind specifically, not the jinn, and this usage is established. The pearl is well known. As for the coral (al-marjān), it is said: it is the small pearls. This was said by Mujāhid, Qatādah, Abū Razīn and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and it is related from ʿAlī.

It is also said: it is the large and fine ones. Ibn Jarīr related this from some of the early scholars, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim related it from al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas, and related it from al-Suddī, from someone who narrated to him, from Ibn ʿAbbās. Similar has been related from ʿAlī, Mujāhid also, and Murrah al-Hamdānī.

It is also said: it is a type of red gem. al-Suddī said, from Abū Mālik, from Masrūq, from ʿAbd Allāh (Ibn Masʿūd), who said: al-marjān is the red bead. Al-Suddī said: it is al-busaḏ (a Persian term).

As for His saying: ﴿and from both you eat tender flesh and extract ornaments which you wear﴾ [Fāṭir: 12], the flesh comes from both the salty and the sweet, but the ornament comes only from the salt, not the sweet.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: never does a drop fall from the sky into the sea and land in a shell except that it becomes a pearl from it. ʿIkrimah said the same, and added: and if it does not fall into a shell, an ʿanbar (ambergris) grows from it. It is related through more than one route from Ibn ʿAbbās something similar.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: Aḥmad ibn Sinān narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī narrated to us, Sufyān narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās who said: when the sky rains, the shells in the sea open their mouths, and whatever falls into them, meaning of the drop, becomes pearl.

Its chain is ṣaḥīḥ (sound). And since the making of this ornament is a blessing upon the people of the earth, He reminded them of it, saying: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And His are the ships, raised high on the sea like mountains﴾, meaning: the ships that run upon the sea. Mujāhid said: whatever ship raises its sail is "munshaʾah" (raised), and whatever does not raise its sail is not munshaʾah. Qatādah said: ﴿al-munshaʾāt﴾ means the created things. Others said: al-munshiʾāt, with a kasra on the shīn, means: those that begin (the journey).

﴿like mountains﴾, that is, like mountains in their size, and what is in them of merchandise and gains transported from region to region and climate to climate, which is of benefit to people in bringing what they need of all kinds of goods. For this reason He said, exalted is He: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?﴾

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: my father narrated to us, Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl narrated to us, Ḥammād ibn Salamah narrated to us, al-ʿArrār ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from ʿUmayrah ibn Saʿd who said: I was with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, on the bank of the Euphrates when a ship came toward us with its sail raised. He spread out his hands and said: Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿And His are the ships, raised high on the sea like mountains﴾. By the One who created it, it runs in its course... I did not kill ʿUthmān, nor did I assist in his killing.

Ibn Kathir says: Allah mentions His creation of man from clay like pottery (ṣalṣāl kal-fakhkhār), and His creation of the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire (mārij min nār), which is the tip of its flame. Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 55, verses 26–30:

The Exalted says that all the people of the earth will pass away and die, all of them, and likewise the people of the heavens, except whom Allah wills. Nothing will remain except His Noble Face. The Lord, exalted and glorified, does not die. Rather, He is the Living who never dies, ever.

Qatadah said: He informed of what He created, then He informed that all of it was [[In manuscript M: "fa-an" (variant reading).]].

In the transmitted supplication: "O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Originator of the heavens and the earth, O Possessor of majesty and honour, there is no god but You. By Your mercy we seek help. Set right for us all our affairs, and do not leave us to ourselves even for the blink of an eye, nor to anyone of Your creation."

Ash-Sha'bi said: When you recite ﴿Everyone upon it will perish﴾, do not stay silent until you recite ﴿And there remains the Face of your Lord, Owner of majesty and honour﴾.

This verse is like His saying: ﴿Everything will perish except His Face﴾ [Al-Qasas: 88]. In this noble verse, He described His Noble Face as ﴿Owner of majesty and honour﴾, meaning He is worthy to be magnified so that He is not disobeyed, and to be obeyed so that He is not opposed. This is like His saying: ﴿And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face﴾ [Al-Kahf: 28], and like His saying, reporting about the charitable: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah's Face﴾ [Al-Insan: 9].

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿Owner of majesty and honour﴾ means the Owner of greatness and pride.

When He informed of the equality of all the people of the earth in death, and that they will return to the Hereafter, where the Owner of majesty and honour will judge them with His just judgment, He said: ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you two deny?﴾

And His saying: ﴿Whoever is in the heavens and the earth asks Him. Every day He is in a matter﴾. This is an announcement of His independence from all else and of the dependence of all creatures upon Him at every moment, and that they ask Him by the tongue of their state and their speech, and that every day He is in a matter.

Al-A'mash related from Mujahid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, regarding ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾: among His matters is that He answers one who calls, or gives to one who asks, or frees one who is captive, or heals one who is sick.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid: Every day He answers one who calls, removes distress, responds to one in need, and forgives a sin.

Ibn Jarir said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Amr al-Ghuzzi related to me, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi related to me, Amr ibn Bakr al-Sakasiki related to me, al-Harith ibn Abdah ibn Rabah al-Ghassani related to us, from his father, from Muneeb ibn Abdullah ibn Muneeb al-Azdi, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾. We said: O Messenger of Allah, what is that matter? He said: "That He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, raises a people, and lowers others." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/79). Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat (no. 3401) and al-Bazzar in his Musnad (no. 2266) also narrated it through Amr ibn Bakr al-Sakasiki, who is abandoned (matruk), from al-Harith ibn Abdah, with the same wording.]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Hisham ibn Ammar and Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Wasiti related to us, both saying: al-Wazir [[In manuscript M: "Abu Razin."]] ibn Subaih al-Thaqafi, Abu Rawh al-Dimashqi, related to us, and the wording is Hisham's, who said: I heard Yunus ibn Maysarah ibn Halbas narrate from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾." He said: "Among His matters is that He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, raises a people, and lowers others." [[Ibn Majah (no. 202) narrated it through Hisham ibn Ammar. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/88): "This is a good chain (isnad), since al-Wazir falls short of the degree of retention and precision."]]

Ibn Asakir narrated it through multiple routes from Hisham ibn Ammar. Then he cited it from the hadith of Abu Hammam al-Walid ibn Shuja', from al-Wazir ibn Subaih, who said: "al-Walid ibn Muslim pointed us to it, from Mutarrif, from al-Sha'bi, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet ﷺ," and he mentioned it. He said: "The sound one is the first," meaning its first chain. [[Tarikh Dimashq (17/771, manuscript section).]]

I say: It has also been transmitted as a statement of Abu al-Darda' (mawquf), as al-Bukhari recorded it in a firm form, making it part of Abu al-Darda's own words. [[Sahih al-Bukhari (8/620, Fath al-Bari). Al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman narrated it connected (mawsul) no. 1102 through Isma'il ibn Abdullah, from Umm al-Darda', from Abu al-Darda', as a mawquf report.]] And Allah knows best.

Al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, Muhammad ibn al-Harith related to us, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Bailamani related to us, from his father, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding ﴿Every day He is in a matter﴾, that he said: "He forgives a sin and removes a distress." [[Musnad al-Bazzar (no. 2268, Kashf al-Astar). Ibn Hajar said: "al-Bailamani is weak (da'if)."]]

Then Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb related to us, Ubaydullah ibn Musa related to us, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali, from Sa'id ibn Jubair, from Ibn Abbas, that Allah created a Preserved Tablet (lawh mahfuz) of white pearl, whose two covers are of red ruby, its pen is light, its book is light, its width is the distance between the heaven and the earth. He looks into it every day three hundred and sixty times, creating in each glance, giving life, causing death, honouring, and humbling, and He does what He wills. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/79).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 55, verses 31–36:

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying ﴿We will attend to you, O two heavy ones﴾: "It is a warning from Allah to the servants, and there is no preoccupation for Allah, for He is free (of concern)." Likewise al-Dahhak said: "This is a warning." Qatada said: "Allah's leisure for His creation has drawn near." Ibn Jurayj said: "﴿We will attend to you﴾ means: We will judge you."

Al-Bukhari said: "We will call you to account, nothing preoccupies Him from anything. This is known in the speech of the Arabs; one says, 'I will surely be free for you,' while he has no preoccupation, meaning, 'I will surely seize you while you are unaware.'"

* *

As for His saying ﴿O two heavy ones﴾: al-Thaqalan (the two heavy ones) are mankind and the jinn, as came in the Sahih (collection): "Everything hears it except the two heavy ones (al-thaqalayn)." In another narration: "except the jinn and mankind." In the hadith of the Trumpet (a prophetic report about the Trumpet): "al-thaqalan are mankind and the jinn." ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond. You will not pass except with authority﴾. That is: you cannot flee from the command and decree of Allah. Rather, He encompasses you, and you cannot escape His judgment or pass beyond His ruling over you. Wherever you go, you will be surrounded. This is in the station of the Gathering, when the angels will encircle the creatures in seven rows from every side, so no one will be able to go anywhere ﴿except with authority﴾, that is, except by the command of Allah. ﴿On that Day man will say, "Where is the escape?" No! There is no refuge. To your Lord on that Day is the place of rest﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:10–12]. And He, exalted, said: ﴿Those who earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is its like, and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. It is as if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein forever﴾ [Yunus 10:27]. For this reason He said: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and molten brass, and you will not be able to defend yourselves﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas: al-Shuwaz is the flame of fire.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn Abbas: al-Shuwaz is smoke.

Mujahid said: it is the green, unbroken flame. Abu Salih said: al-Shuwaz is the flame that is above the fire and below the smoke. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿a flame of fire﴾ is a torrent of fire.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and molten brass﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿nuhas﴾ is the smoke of the fire. The same was related from Abu Salih, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Abu Sinan.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: The Arabs call smoke nuhas (with the nun vowelled with a dammah or a kasrah), and the readers are unanimous on the dammah. From the use of nuhas in the sense of smoke is the verse of Nabigha Ja'da:

It shines like the light of a lamp of ... it, Allah has not placed brass in it.

He means: smoke. Thus he said.

Al-Tabarani related through the route of Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas about al-Shuwaz, and he said: "It is the flame that has no smoke with it." He then asked him for evidence from the language, so he recited to him the verse of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt about Hassan:

Is there no one who will convey to Hassan from me, a message that creeps toward Ukaz,

Was not your father among us a smith, at the place of the singing-girls, so ask in the vessels,

A Yemeni who keeps working the bellows, and blows continuously the flame of the shuwaz.

He said: "You have spoken truly." Then he asked: "What is nuhas?" He said: "It is smoke that has no flame." He asked: "Does the Arabs know it?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard the Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan saying:"

It shines like the light of a lamp of the olive oil ... Allah has not placed brass in it.

(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/305), in which Juwaybir appears; he is abandoned (matruk) and did not meet Ibn Abbas.)

Mujahid said: al-Nuhas is the yellow brass, melted and poured over their heads. Qatada said the same. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿nuhas﴾ is a torrent of brass.

The meaning, according to every opinion, is: if you were to flee on the Day of Resurrection, the angels and the guards of Hell would turn you back by sending down upon you flames of fire and molten brass, so that you would return. For this reason He said: ﴿So you will not be able to defend yourselves. Then which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 55, verses 31–36:

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas concerning His saying ﴿We will attend to you, O two heavy ones﴾: "It is a warning from Allah to the servants, and there is no preoccupation for Allah, for He is free (of concern)." Likewise al-Dahhak said: "This is a warning." Qatada said: "Allah's leisure for His creation has drawn near." Ibn Jurayj said: "﴿We will attend to you﴾ means: We will judge you."

Al-Bukhari said: "We will call you to account, nothing preoccupies Him from anything. This is known in the speech of the Arabs; one says, 'I will surely be free for you,' while he has no preoccupation, meaning, 'I will surely seize you while you are unaware.'"

* *

As for His saying ﴿O two heavy ones﴾: al-Thaqalan (the two heavy ones) are mankind and the jinn, as came in the Sahih (collection): "Everything hears it except the two heavy ones (al-thaqalayn)." In another narration: "except the jinn and mankind." In the hadith of the Trumpet (a prophetic report about the Trumpet): "al-thaqalan are mankind and the jinn." ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, then pass beyond. You will not pass except with authority﴾. That is: you cannot flee from the command and decree of Allah. Rather, He encompasses you, and you cannot escape His judgment or pass beyond His ruling over you. Wherever you go, you will be surrounded. This is in the station of the Gathering, when the angels will encircle the creatures in seven rows from every side, so no one will be able to go anywhere ﴿except with authority﴾, that is, except by the command of Allah. ﴿On that Day man will say, "Where is the escape?" No! There is no refuge. To your Lord on that Day is the place of rest﴾ [al-Qiyamah 75:10–12]. And He, exalted, said: ﴿Those who earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is its like, and humiliation will cover them. They will have no protector from Allah. It is as if their faces were covered with pieces of the dark night. Those are the companions of the Fire, they will abide therein forever﴾ [Yunus 10:27]. For this reason He said: ﴿There will be sent against you both a flame of fire and molten brass, and you will not be able to defend yourselves﴾.

Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas: al-Shuwaz is the flame of fire.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn Abbas: al-Shuwaz is smoke.

Mujahid said: it is the green, unbroken flame. Abu Salih said: al-Shuwaz is the flame that is above the fire and below the smoke. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿a flame of fire﴾ is a torrent of fire.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and molten brass﴾: Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿nuhas﴾ is the smoke of the fire. The same was related from Abu Salih, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Abu Sinan.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: The Arabs call smoke nuhas (with the nun vowelled with a dammah or a kasrah), and the readers are unanimous on the dammah. From the use of nuhas in the sense of smoke is the verse of Nabigha Ja'da:

It shines like the light of a lamp of ... it, Allah has not placed brass in it.

He means: smoke. Thus he said.

Al-Tabarani related through the route of Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq asked Ibn Abbas about al-Shuwaz, and he said: "It is the flame that has no smoke with it." He then asked him for evidence from the language, so he recited to him the verse of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt about Hassan:

Is there no one who will convey to Hassan from me, a message that creeps toward Ukaz,

Was not your father among us a smith, at the place of the singing-girls, so ask in the vessels,

A Yemeni who keeps working the bellows, and blows continuously the flame of the shuwaz.

He said: "You have spoken truly." Then he asked: "What is nuhas?" He said: "It is smoke that has no flame." He asked: "Does the Arabs know it?" He said: "Yes. Have you not heard the Nabigha of Banu Dhubyan saying:"

It shines like the light of a lamp of the olive oil ... Allah has not placed brass in it.

(Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/305), in which Juwaybir appears; he is abandoned (matruk) and did not meet Ibn Abbas.)

For this reason He said: ﴿So you will not be able to defend yourselves. Then which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And when the sky is split open﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, as this verse indicates together with similar verses that carry the same meaning, such as His saying: ﴿And the sky will be split open, for it will that Day be frail﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:16], His saying: ﴿And the Day the sky is split open with clouds, and the angels are sent down in descent﴾ [al-Furqan 25:25], and His saying: ﴿When the sky is split open, and it hearkens to its Lord, and it is obliged to do so﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 84:1-2].

His saying: ﴿it became rose-red like oil﴾, meaning it melts as the dregs (al-durdi) and silver melt in the smelting, and it changes color as the dyes with which things are smeared change color, sometimes red, yellow, blue and green. This is from the severity of the matter and the great terror of the Day of Resurrection. Imam Ahmad said:

Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Sahba' narrated to us, Nafi' Abu Ghalib al-Bahili narrated to us, Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection while the sky is dripping upon them." [al-Musnad 3/226]

Al-Jawhari said: al-tash is light rain.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿rose-red like oil﴾: it is red leather. Abu Kudaynah said, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿it became rose-red like oil﴾: like a rose-colored horse. Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: its color changed. Abu Salih said: like a rose-colored mule, then after that it became like oil.

Al-Baghawi and others related that the rose-colored horse is yellow in spring and red in winter, and when the cold intensifies its color becomes dusky.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it will be (of) various colors. Al-Suddi said: it will be like the color of a rose-colored mule, and it will be like the molten metal (al-muhl), like the dregs of olive oil. Mujahid said: ﴿like oil﴾ means like the colors of oil. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: like the color of rose oil in yellowness. Qatadah said: it is green today, and on that Day its color will turn to red, a day of many colors. Abu al-Jawza' said: in the clarity of oil. Abu Salih, [[Addition from A.]] Ibn Jurayj said: the sky becomes like melting oil, and that is when the heat of Hell touches it.

* *

His saying: ﴿So on that Day no one will be questioned about his sin, neither man nor jinn﴾. This is like His saying: ﴿This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuses﴾ [al-Mursalat 77:35-36]. This refers to one state, and there is another state in which the creatures will be questioned about all their deeds. God says: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr 15:92-93]. Regarding this, Qatadah said about ﴿So on that Day no one will be questioned about his sin, neither man nor jinn﴾: there was a questioning, then mouths were sealed, and their hands and feet spoke of what they used to do.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas: He will not ask them, "Did you do such and such?" because He knows that better than they do, but He will say, "Why did you do such and such?" This is a second opinion.

Mujahid said regarding this verse: the angels will not question about the criminal; they are recognized by their marks.

This is a third opinion. It seems that this is after they are ordered to the Fire. At that time they will not be questioned about their sins, but they will be dragged to it and thrown into it, as God says: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks﴾, meaning by signs that appear upon them.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: they will recognize them by the blackening of faces and the blueness of eyes.

I say: this is like how the believers are recognized by the white blaze and the white markings from the traces of ablution.

* *

His saying: ﴿So they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet﴾, meaning the Zabaniyah (the angels of punishment) gather his forelock together with his feet, and they throw him into the Fire in that manner.

Al-A'mash said, from Ibn 'Abbas: he is seized by his forelock and his foot, and he is broken as firewood is broken in the oven.

Al-Dahhak said: his forelock and his two feet are joined together with a chain behind his back.

Al-Suddi said: the forelock of the disbeliever and his feet are joined together, his forelock is tied to his foot, and his back is twisted.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Tawbah al-Rabi' ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Mu'awiyah ibn Sallam narrated to us, from his brother Zayd ibn Sallam, that he heard Abu Sallam, meaning his grandfather, say: 'Abd al-Rahman informed me, a man from Kindah narrated to me, who said: I came to 'A'ishah, entered upon her, and there was a curtain between me and her. I said: Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) tell you that there will come upon him a time when he will have no power to intercede for anyone? She said: Yes. I asked him about this while he and I were under one garment. He said: "Yes, when the Sirat (bridge) is laid down, and I will have no power to intercede for anyone on it until I know where I will be led. And on the Day when some faces will be white and some faces will be black, until I see what will be done to me, or he said: what will be revealed to me. And at the bridge when it becomes sharp and hot." She said: What is meant by sharp and hot? He said: "It becomes sharp until it is like the edge of a sword, and it becomes hot until it is like a live coal. As for the believer, it lets him cross without harming him. As for the hypocrite, he will cling until, when he reaches its middle, he falls from his foot, and he flails with his hand toward his feet, and the Zabaniyah strike him with a hook in his forelock and his foot and throw him into Hell, and he falls into it for a distance of fifty years." I said: What is the weight of the man? She said: The weight of ten fat pregnant she-camels. So on that Day the criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.

This is a very strange hadith; some of its wording is objectionable in its attribution to the Prophet, and there is in its chain one who is unnamed, and such a narration cannot be used as evidence. [[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/704), from a man from Kindah, in similar wording.]] And God knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny﴾, meaning: this is the Fire which you used to deny the existence of. Here it is, present, and you are witnessing it with your own eyes. This is said to them as rebuke, reproach, belittlement and humiliation.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding, boiling water﴾, meaning: at times they will be tormented in the blazing Hell, and at times they will be given to drink from the scalding water, which is the drink like molten copper that cuts the intestines and the bowels. This is like His saying: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains; they will be dragged through scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned﴾ [Ghafir 40:71-72].

* *

His saying: ﴿boiling water (ana)﴾, meaning: hot, having reached the utmost in heat, so that it cannot be endured because of its intensity.

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying ﴿they will go around between it and scalding, boiling water﴾: it has reached its boiling point and its heat has intensified. Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Thawri and al-Suddi said the same.

Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since God created the heavens and the earth. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the servant is taken and his forelock is moved in that scalding water until the flesh melts and only the bone and the two eyes remain in the head. This is like what God says: ﴿in scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned﴾. "Hameem an-aan" means: the very hot. And there is another report from al-Qurazi: ﴿hameem aan﴾ means: present. This is also the opinion of Ibn Zayd. The meaning "present" does not contradict what was narrated from al-Qurazi first, that it means hot, just as God says: ﴿they will be given to drink from a spring that is boiling (aniyah)﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:5], meaning very hot and so intense that it cannot be endured. Likewise His saying: ﴿not waiting for its ripening (inah)﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:53], meaning its becoming ready and cooked. So His saying ﴿hameem aan﴾ means: very hot water.

I asked him about this while he and I were under one garment. He said: "Yes, when the Sirat (bridge) is laid down, and I will have no power to intercede for anyone on it until I know where I will be led. And on the Day when some faces will be white and some faces will be black, until I see what will be done to me, or he said: what will be revealed to me. And at the bridge when it becomes sharp and hot." She said: What is meant by sharp and hot? He said: "It becomes sharp until it is like the edge of a sword, and it becomes hot until it is like a live coal. As for the believer, it lets him cross without harming him. As for the hypocrite, he will cling until, when he reaches its middle, he falls from his foot, and he flails with his hand toward his feet, and the Zabaniyah strike him with a hook in his forelock and his foot and throw him into Hell, and he falls into it for a distance of fifty years." I said: What is the weight of the man? She said: The weight of ten fat pregnant she-camels. So on that Day the criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.

This is a very strange hadith; some of its wording is objectionable in its attribution to the Prophet, and there is in its chain one who is unnamed, and such a narration cannot be used as evidence. [[Narrated by 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/704), from a man from Kindah, in similar wording.]] And God knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿This is Hell, which the criminals used to deny﴾, meaning: this is the Fire which you used to deny the existence of. Here it is, present, and you are witnessing it with your own eyes. This is said to them as rebuke, reproach, belittlement and humiliation.

* *

His saying: ﴿They will go around between it and scalding, boiling water﴾, meaning: at times they will be tormented in the blazing Hell, and at times they will be given to drink from the scalding water, which is the drink like molten copper that cuts the intestines and the bowels. This is like His saying: ﴿When the shackles are around their necks and the chains; they will be dragged through scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned﴾ [Ghafir 40:71-72].

* *

His saying: ﴿boiling water (ana)﴾, meaning: hot, having reached the utmost in heat, so that it cannot be endured because of its intensity.

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying ﴿they will go around between it and scalding, boiling water﴾: it has reached its boiling point and its heat has intensified. Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, al-Thawri and al-Suddi said the same.

Qatadah said: its cooking has been going on since God created the heavens and the earth. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: the servant is taken and his forelock is moved in that scalding water until the flesh melts and only the bone and the two eyes remain in the head. This is like what God says: ﴿in scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned﴾. "Hameem an-aan" means: the very hot. And there is another report from al-Qurazi: ﴿hameem aan﴾ means: present. This is also the opinion of Ibn Zayd. The meaning "present" does not contradict what was narrated from al-Qurazi first, that it means hot, just as God says: ﴿they will be given to drink from a spring that is boiling (aniyah)﴾ [al-Ghashiyah 88:5], meaning very hot and so intense that it cannot be endured. Likewise His saying: ﴿not waiting for its ripening (inah)﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:53], meaning its becoming ready and cooked. So His saying ﴿hameem aan﴾ means: very hot water.

When God had mentioned the punishment of the disobedient criminals and the blessings of the pious, which are from His grace, mercy, justice and kindness toward His creation, and when His warning to them of His punishment and might was something that would restrain them from the polytheism, the disobedience and other things in which they were engaged, He said, enumerating His favors to His creatures: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

Ibn Shawdhab and ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani said: This verse, "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens," was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

He said: He repented for a day and a night after he had spoken these words, so God accepted his repentance and admitted him into Paradise.

The correct view is that this verse is general, as Ibn ʿAbbas and others said. The Exalted says: "But for him who fears the standing before God on the Day of Resurrection," ﴿and restrains the soul from its desire﴾ [al-Naziʿat 79:40], and does not transgress, nor prefer the worldly life, and knows that the Hereafter is better and more enduring. Nothing stands between the people and looking at their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, except the cloak of pride over His face, in the Garden of Eden."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it, all of the Six Books except Abu Dawud, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, with the same chain.

He said: "Even if Abu al-Darda's nose is rubbed in the dust."

﴿In them are two flowing springs﴾, meaning they flow to water those trees and branches, so that they bear fruit of all colours. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: One of them is called "Tasnim," and the other "Salsabil."

ʿAtiyyah said: One of them is of water that does not change, and the other is of wine, delicious to the drinkers.

Hence He said after this: ﴿In them are two kinds of every fruit﴾, meaning of all kinds of fruits, some known to them and others of a different sort, and others no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: There is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world but that it is in Paradise, even the colocynth.

Ibn ʿAbbas also said: Nothing in this world is like what is in the Hereafter except the names; that is, there is a great difference between them and a clear distinction in excellence.

Ibn Shawdhab and ʿAtaʾ al-Khurasani said: This verse, "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens," was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Musaffa narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from ʿAtiyyah ibn Qays, regarding His words, "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens": it was revealed concerning the man who said, "Burn me with fire, perhaps I may lead God astray." He said: He repented for a day and a night after he had spoken these words, so God accepted his repentance and admitted him into Paradise.

The correct view is that this verse is general, as Ibn ʿAbbas and others said. The Exalted says: "But for him who fears the standing before God on the Day of Resurrection," ﴿and restrains the soul from its desire﴾ [al-Naziʿat 79:40], and does not transgress, nor prefer the worldly life, and knows that the Hereafter is better and more enduring. He performs God's obligations and avoids His prohibitions. For him, on the Day of Resurrection, with his Lord, are two gardens, as al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, stated.

ʿAbdullah ibn Abi al-Aswad narrated to us, ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbd al-Samad al-ʿAmmi narrated to us, Abu ʿImran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdullah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Two gardens of silver, their vessels and whatever is in them; and two gardens of gold, their vessels and whatever is in them. Nothing stands between the people and looking at their Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, except the cloak of pride over His face, in the Garden of Eden."

Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it, all of the Six Books except Abu Dawud, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, with the same chain.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Thabit, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, from his father (Hammad said: I do not know it except as traced to the Prophet (ﷺ)), concerning His words: "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens," and His words: "And beyond these two are two gardens." He said: Two gardens of gold for those brought near, and two gardens of silver for the people of the right hand.

Ibn Jarir said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Harmalah, from ʿAta' ibn Yasar, Abu al-Darda' informed me that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited one day this verse: "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens." I said: "Even if he commits fornication or steals?" He recited: "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens." I said: "Even if he commits fornication and even if he steals?" He recited: "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens." I said: "Even if he commits fornication and even if he steals, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Even if Abu al-Darda's nose is rubbed in the dust."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Abi Harmalah, with the same chain. Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from Mu'ammal ibn Hisham, from Isma'il, from al-Juraybi, from Musa, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from Abu al-Darda', with the same. It has also been narrated as a statement of Abu al-Darda' (mawquf). It is reported from him that he said: Whoever fears the standing before his Lord does not commit fornication and does not steal.

This verse is general regarding both humans and jinn. It is among the clearest proofs that the jinn enter Paradise if they believe and are mindful of God. For this reason God bestowed favour upon both species (the two weighty ones) with this reward, saying: "But for him who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens. So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?"

Then He described these two gardens, saying: ﴿having branches﴾, meaning branches that are lush and beautiful, bearing every ripe and excellent fruit. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ Thus ʿAta' al-Khurasani and a group said: al-Afnan are the branches of trees, some of which touch one another.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, Muslim ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, ʿAbdullah ibn al-Nuʿman narrated to us, I heard ʿIkrimah say regarding "having branches": it means the shade of the branches upon the walls. Have you not heard the poet's saying:

"What stirred your longing is the cooing of a dove, calling on the branches of the boughs, calling doves..."

"It calls to the father of two chicks, meeting a hungry one with two talons, a falcon, a qata."

Al-Baghawi related from Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi that it means the straight branch, long in height.

He said: Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated to us, ʿAta' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding "having branches": "having colours."

He said: It has been related from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, Khusayf, al-Nadr ibn ʿArabi and Abu Sinan the same. The meaning of this view is that in them are various kinds of delights, and al-Tabari preferred it.

ʿAta' said: each branch combines various kinds of fruit. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: "having branches" means wide of courtyard.

All these views are correct, and there is no contradiction between them, and God knows best. Qatadah said: "having branches" indicates their vastness, their excellence and their superiority over all others.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yahya ibn ʿAbbad ibn ʿAbdullah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from Asma' (who said): I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) mention the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, and he said: "A rider could travel in the shade of one of its branches for a hundred years, or he said: a hundred riders could shelter in the shade of one of its branches. In it are golden butterflies, and its fruit is like large jars."

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bukayr, with the same. He said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."

﴿In them are two flowing springs﴾, meaning they flow to water those trees and branches, so that they bear fruit of all colours. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ Al-Hasan al-Basri said: One of them is called "Tasnim," and the other "Salsabil."

Hence He said after this: ﴿In them are two kinds of every fruit﴾, meaning of all kinds of fruits, some known to them and others of a different sort, and others no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord will you both deny?﴾

Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated, from his father, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: There is no sweet or bitter fruit in this world but that it is in Paradise, even the colocynth.

Ibn ʿAbbas also said: Nothing in this world is like what is in the Hereafter except the names; that is, there is a great difference between them and a clear distinction in excellence.

God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Reclining﴾, meaning the people of Paradise. Here, reclining means lying down, and it is also said to mean sitting in the posture of tarabbu' (sitting cross-legged on the floor). ﴿On couches whose linings are of silk brocade (istabraq)﴾. Istabraq is the thick kind of dibaj (silk brocade). This was said by 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and Qatadah.

Abu 'Imran al-Jawni said: it is dibaj embroidered with gold. Thus He draws attention to the nobility of the outer surface through the nobility of the lining. This is an instance of alerting to the higher by means of the lesser.

Abu Ishaq narrated from Hubayrah ibn Yarim, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "These are the linings. How then would you be if you saw the outer surfaces?"

Malik ibn Dinar said: "Their linings are of istabraq, and their outer surfaces are of light."

Sufyan al-Thawri, or Sharik, said: "Their linings are of istabraq, and their outer surfaces are of solid light."

al-Qasim ibn Muhammad [in M: "Mukhaymir"] said: "Their linings are of istabraq, and their outer surfaces are of mercy."

Ibn Shawdhab, from Abu 'Abdullah al-Shami, said: "God mentioned the linings and did not mention the outer surfaces. Upon the outer surfaces are the mahabis (coverings), and no one knows what is beneath the mahabis except God." Al-Imam Ibn Abi Hatim related all of this.

﴿And the fruit of the two gardens is near﴾, meaning its fruit is close to them. Whenever they wish, they may take it, in whatever position they are in, as He said: ﴿Its clusters hang low﴾ [al-Haqqah 69:23], and He said: ﴿And near over them will be its shade, and its fruit will be lowered in readiness﴾ [al-Insan 76:14], meaning it is not withheld from whoever reaches for it; rather, it lowers itself to him from its branches. ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾

When He mentioned the couches and their greatness, He said after that: ﴿Therein﴾, meaning in the couches, ﴿are those who restrain their gaze﴾, meaning who lower their eyes from other than their husbands, so they see nothing more beautiful in Paradise than their husbands. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah, 'Ata' al-Khurasani and Ibn Zayd.

It has been related that one of them says to her husband: "By God, I see nothing in Paradise more beautiful than you, and there is nothing in Paradise more beloved to me than you. Praise be to God who made you for me and made me for you."

Artah ibn al-Mundhir said: Damrah ibn Habib was asked, "Do the jinn enter Paradise?" He said: "Yes, and they marry. The jinn have female jinn, and mankind have female humans." This is His saying: ﴿No man or jinn has touched them before them. So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾

As for the ruby, it is a stone; if you were to pass a thread through it and then make it clear, you would see it from behind."

Al-Imam Ahmad alone narrated it through this route [al-Musnad 2/345]. Muslim also related it from the hadith of Isma'il ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "Whether they were boasting or recalling, the men said: 'Are there more men or women in Paradise?' Abu Hurayrah said: 'Did not Abu al-Qasim (ﷺ) say: "The first group to enter Paradise will be in the form of the moon on the night of the full moon, and those after them will be upon the brightest star in the sky. Each man among them will have two wives, through whom the marrow of their shins can be seen beyond the flesh, and there is no bachelor in Paradise"?'" [Sahih Muslim no. 2834].

This hadith is recorded in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Hammam ibn Munabbih and Abu Zur'ah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 3245; Sahih Muslim no. 2834].

Al-Imam Ahmad also said: Abu al-Nadr related to us, Muhammad ibn Talhah related to us, from Humayd, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A morning or evening spent in the way of Allah is better than the world and whatever is in it. And the bow-length of one of you—or the place of his whip [in M: 'qadduh'; in A: 'qadamuh'], meaning his whip—in Paradise is better than the world and whatever is in it. And if a woman of the women of the people of Paradise looked down upon the earth, she would fill what is between them with fragrance and make what is between them fragrant, and her headscarf upon her head is better than the world and whatever is in it."

Al-Bukhari related it from the hadith of Abu Ishaq, from Humayd, from Anas, in similar words [al-Musnad 3/141; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 2796].

[Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi 7/456; in it is Bishr al-Asbahani, who narrates from al-Zubayr ibn 'Adi from Anas with a fabricated copy (nuskhah mawdu'ah)].

Since what has been mentioned contains great blessings which no deed can match, but are pure bounty and grace, He said after all of this: ﴿So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Among what relates to His saying: ﴿And for those who fear the standing before their Lord are two gardens﴾, is what al-Tirmidhi and al-Baghawi related from the hadith of Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Abu 'Aqil al-Thaqafi, from Abu Farwah Yazid ibn Sinan al-Rahawi, from Bukayr ibn Fayrouz [in A: "Fayrouz al-Daylami"], from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fears sets out early in the night, and whoever sets out early reaches the destination. Indeed, the commodity of Allah is precious; indeed, the commodity of Allah is Paradise."

Then al-Tirmidhi said: "It is gharib (unusual); we do not know it except from the hadith of Abu al-Nadr" [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2450; Tafsir al-Baghawi 7/451].

Al-Baghawi also related from the hadith of 'Ali ibn Hujr, from Isma'il ibn Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn Abi Harmalah, mawla of Huwaytib ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu al-Darda', that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) preaching from the pulpit, reciting: ﴿And for those who fear the standing before their Lord are two gardens.﴾ I said: "And even if he commits adultery and theft, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿And for those who fear the standing before their Lord are two gardens.﴾ I said a second time: "And even if he commits adultery and theft, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿And for those who fear the standing before their Lord are two gardens.﴾ I said a third time: "And even if he commits adultery and theft, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Even so, may the nose of Abu al-Darda' be rubbed in the dust" [Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi 7/452].

These two gardens are below the previous two in rank, virtue, and standing, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾.

It has already been mentioned in a hadith: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them are of gold, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them are of silver. The first two are for those brought near (to Allah), and the latter two are for the companions of the right hand."[[In M: "فالأولتان" (the first two).]][[In M: "والأخيرتان" (the latter two).]]

Abu Musa said: "Two gardens of gold are for those brought near, and two gardens of silver are for the companions of the right hand."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾: "Besides them in degree." Ibn Zayd said: "Besides them in excellence."

The evidence for the superiority of the first two over the latter two is several-fold. First: He described the first two before these two, and placement first indicates special concern. Then He said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾. This clearly shows the superiority of what comes first and its elevation over the second.

Also, there He said: ﴿Both having branches﴾, that is, boughs or varieties of pleasures. Here He said: ﴿Dark green﴾, that is, deep green from the intensity of irrigation.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿Dark green﴾: "They have become black from the greenness, due to the intensity of irrigation with water."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Dark green﴾: he said, "Greenish-green." It is also narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, 'Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), 'Ata', 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafi', and Sufyan al-Thawri, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿Dark green﴾: "Full of greenness." Qatada said: "Greenish from irrigation, lush." There is no doubt about the freshness of the branches on trees that are interwoven with one another.

There He said: ﴿In both of them are two springs flowing﴾, and here He said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, "overflowing." Flowing is stronger than gushing.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾ means "full, never ceasing."

There He said: ﴿In both of them, of every fruit, two kinds﴾, and here He said: ﴿In both of them are fruit, and date palms and pomegranates﴾. There is no doubt that the first is more general and greater in number and variety, since "fruit" (fakiha) here is indefinite in an affirmative context and does not indicate all-inclusiveness. For this reason, His words ﴿and date palms and pomegranates﴾ are explained as the mention of a particular after a general, as al-Bukhari and others affirmed. The date palm and the pomegranate are singled out for mention only because of their nobility over other fruits.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Mukhariq narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates." They said: "Will they eat as they eat in this world?" He said: "Yes, and multiplied." They said: "Will they relieve themselves?" He said: "No, but they will perspire and exude, and Allah will remove whatever discomfort is in their bellies."[[Recorded in al-Muntakhab, no. 35, and in it is Husayn ibn 'Umar, who is abandoned (matruk).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The date palms of Paradise: their palm fronds are clothing for the people of Paradise, from which are their cut garments and their robes. Their spathes are red gold, their trunks are green emerald, their fruit is sweeter than honey and softer than butter, and it has no pit."

And my father narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salama, narrated to us, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I looked at Paradise, and a pomegranate from its pomegranates was like a saddled camel."[[Recorded by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, as cited in the takhrij of the Ihya' (6/2787), and by Ibn 'Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as cited in its abridgment (5/462), through the route of Abu Harun al-'Abdi. Abu Harun al-'Abdi, whose name is 'Umara ibn Juwayn, was declared a liar by some of the imams.]]

Then He said: ﴿In them are good, beautiful ones﴾. It was said: the meaning is many good things in Paradise, said by Qatada. It was also said: "good ones" is the plural of "khayyira," which is a righteous woman of good character and good appearance, said by the majority. It has been narrated with a elevated chain (marfu') from Umm Salama.[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/367) at length, and in it is Sulayman ibn Abi Karima, who is weak.]] In another hadith, which we will cite in the commentary on surah "al-Waqi'a" (on verses 35–38 of the same surah), the Hur al-'In sing: "We are the good, beautiful ones; we were created for noble husbands." For this reason, some read: "fihinna khayyarat," with shaddah (doubling), ﴿hisan﴾ (beautiful). ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾. There He said: ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾. There is no doubt that she who restrains her own gaze is more excellent than she who is made to restrain, even though all of them are veiled.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah who said: "For every Muslim there is a wife,[[The word "khayyira" is used here.]] and for every wife there is a tent, and for every tent there are four doors. Every day a gift, honor, and present that had not been before enters upon them: neither lively-mannered nor hot-tempered, neither bad-breathed nor foul-smelling, dark-eyed Hur, as if they were hidden eggs."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the pavilions﴾, al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tent of hollow pearl, its width is sixty miles, and in every corner of it are people whom the others do not see; the believers circulate among them."

He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and he said: "thirty miles."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4879) and (3243).]] Muslim also recorded it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and his wording is: "Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollow pearl, its length is sixty miles. The believer has people in it, and the believer circulates among them, but they do not see one another."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2838).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, Khulayd al-'Asri informed me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The tent is a single pearl, in which there are seventy doors of pearl."

And my father narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Abi Fatima narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾, and he said: "[In] pavilions of pearl, and in Paradise is one tent of a pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, upon it are four thousand gold doors."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and a dome of pearl, emerald, and ruby is set up for him, as wide as the distance between al-Jabiya and San'a'."

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2562), and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Rushdayn." Rushdayn was not alone in it, but Ibn Wahb followed him, as here, and in its chain is Darraj, who narrates strange reports (manakir) from Abu al-Haytham.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾: the same as previously stated, except that He added in describing the first ones the words ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?

* *

As for His words ﴿reclining on green cushions and beautiful rich carpets﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-rafraf: the cushions (al-mahabis)." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others: they are the mahabis. Al-'Ala' ibn Badr said: "Al-rafraf is over the couch, in the form of the hanging mahabis."

'Asim al-Jahdari said regarding ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: it means "the cushions." This is also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri in one narration from him.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: "The rafraf: the gardens of Paradise."

* *
