Also in another hadith: "Indeed, among the veneration of Allah is honouring the grey-haired Muslim, and the bearer of the Qur'an (in some copies: 'the dhikr') who is neither excessive in it nor neglectful of it, and the just ruler." (Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4843, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/163), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Yusuf al-Jizi (in the original and the rest of the copies: "al-Harbi"; the correction is from Abu Ya'la) narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording. (Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/445) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3522.)

Ibn Tahir said: "Rawh ibn Ubadah has also followed Mu'ammal in this, and Rawh is a trustworthy memorizer."
It was transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (3/396), via Rawh ibn Ubadah from Hammad ibn Salamah from...

Then (al-Tirmidhi) said: Mu'ammal erred in it; it is gharib (strange) and not mahfuz (preserved). Rather, this is narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan al-Maqdisi, from Rabi'ah ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording. (Musnad (4/177) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11563.)

Al-Jawhari said: "Alladha fulan bi-fulan" means: when he clung to him (persistently).

The saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour" means: keep to it (iltizam). It is also said: al-ilzaz is al-ilhah (insistence).

I say: both are close to each other, and Allah knows best; it means persistence, constancy, and insistence. In Sahih Muslim and the Four Sunan, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the salam, he would not sit except for as long as it takes to say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." (Sahih Muslim no. 592; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1512; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 298; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/69); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 924.)

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Rahman, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace].

These two gardens are below the previous two in rank, virtue, and standing, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾.

It has already been mentioned in a hadith: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them are of gold, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them are of silver. The first two are for those brought near (to Allah), and the latter two are for the companions of the right hand."[[In M: "فالأولتان" (the first two).]][[In M: "والأخيرتان" (the latter two).]]

Abu Musa said: "Two gardens of gold are for those brought near, and two gardens of silver are for the companions of the right hand."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾: "Besides them in degree." Ibn Zayd said: "Besides them in excellence."

The evidence for the superiority of the first two over the latter two is several-fold. First: He described the first two before these two, and placement first indicates special concern. Then He said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾. This clearly shows the superiority of what comes first and its elevation over the second.

Also, there He said: ﴿Both having branches﴾, that is, boughs or varieties of pleasures. Here He said: ﴿Dark green﴾, that is, deep green from the intensity of irrigation.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿Dark green﴾: "They have become black from the greenness, due to the intensity of irrigation with water."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Dark green﴾: he said, "Greenish-green." It is also narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, 'Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), 'Ata', 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafi', and Sufyan al-Thawri, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿Dark green﴾: "Full of greenness." Qatada said: "Greenish from irrigation, lush." There is no doubt about the freshness of the branches on trees that are interwoven with one another.

There He said: ﴿In both of them are two springs flowing﴾, and here He said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, "overflowing." Flowing is stronger than gushing.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾ means "full, never ceasing."

There He said: ﴿In both of them, of every fruit, two kinds﴾, and here He said: ﴿In both of them are fruit, and date palms and pomegranates﴾. There is no doubt that the first is more general and greater in number and variety, since "fruit" (fakiha) here is indefinite in an affirmative context and does not indicate all-inclusiveness. For this reason, His words ﴿and date palms and pomegranates﴾ are explained as the mention of a particular after a general, as al-Bukhari and others affirmed. The date palm and the pomegranate are singled out for mention only because of their nobility over other fruits.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Mukhariq narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates." They said: "Will they eat as they eat in this world?" He said: "Yes, and multiplied." They said: "Will they relieve themselves?" He said: "No, but they will perspire and exude, and Allah will remove whatever discomfort is in their bellies."[[Recorded in al-Muntakhab, no. 35, and in it is Husayn ibn 'Umar, who is abandoned (matruk).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The date palms of Paradise: their palm fronds are clothing for the people of Paradise, from which are their cut garments and their robes. Their spathes are red gold, their trunks are green emerald, their fruit is sweeter than honey and softer than butter, and it has no pit."

And my father narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salama, narrated to us, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I looked at Paradise, and a pomegranate from its pomegranates was like a saddled camel."[[Recorded by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, as cited in the takhrij of the Ihya' (6/2787), and by Ibn 'Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as cited in its abridgment (5/462), through the route of Abu Harun al-'Abdi. Abu Harun al-'Abdi, whose name is 'Umara ibn Juwayn, was declared a liar by some of the imams.]]

Then He said: ﴿In them are good, beautiful ones﴾. It was said: the meaning is many good things in Paradise, said by Qatada. It was also said: "good ones" is the plural of "khayyira," which is a righteous woman of good character and good appearance, said by the majority. It has been narrated with a elevated chain (marfu') from Umm Salama.[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/367) at length, and in it is Sulayman ibn Abi Karima, who is weak.]] In another hadith, which we will cite in the commentary on surah "al-Waqi'a" (on verses 35–38 of the same surah), the Hur al-'In sing: "We are the good, beautiful ones; we were created for noble husbands." For this reason, some read: "fihinna khayyarat," with shaddah (doubling), ﴿hisan﴾ (beautiful). ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾. There He said: ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾. There is no doubt that she who restrains her own gaze is more excellent than she who is made to restrain, even though all of them are veiled.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah who said: "For every Muslim there is a wife,[[The word "khayyira" is used here.]] and for every wife there is a tent, and for every tent there are four doors. Every day a gift, honor, and present that had not been before enters upon them: neither lively-mannered nor hot-tempered, neither bad-breathed nor foul-smelling, dark-eyed Hur, as if they were hidden eggs."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the pavilions﴾, al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tent of hollow pearl, its width is sixty miles, and in every corner of it are people whom the others do not see; the believers circulate among them."

He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and he said: "thirty miles."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4879) and (3243).]] Muslim also recorded it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and his wording is: "Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollow pearl, its length is sixty miles. The believer has people in it, and the believer circulates among them, but they do not see one another."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2838).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, Khulayd al-'Asri informed me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The tent is a single pearl, in which there are seventy doors of pearl."

And my father narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Abi Fatima narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾, and he said: "[In] pavilions of pearl, and in Paradise is one tent of a pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, upon it are four thousand gold doors."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and a dome of pearl, emerald, and ruby is set up for him, as wide as the distance between al-Jabiya and San'a'."

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2562), and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Rushdayn." Rushdayn was not alone in it, but Ibn Wahb followed him, as here, and in its chain is Darraj, who narrates strange reports (manakir) from Abu al-Haytham.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾: the same as previously stated, except that He added in describing the first ones the words ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?

* *

As for His words ﴿reclining on green cushions and beautiful rich carpets﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-rafraf: the cushions (al-mahabis)." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others: they are the mahabis. Al-'Ala' ibn Badr said: "Al-rafraf is over the couch, in the form of the hanging mahabis."

'Asim al-Jahdari said regarding ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: it means "the cushions." This is also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri in one narration from him.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: "The rafraf: the gardens of Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: "Al-'abqari: the zarabi (rugs/carpets)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the finest zarabi," meaning their best quality.

Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: brocade (dibaj)."

al-Hasan al-Basri was asked about His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾ and said: "They are the carpets of the people of Paradise—may you have no father—so seek them." It is also narrated from al-Hasan, in one report, that they are "the cushions (al-marafiq)." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-'abqari: red, yellow, and green." Al-'Ala' ibn Zayd was asked about al-'abqari and said: "The carpets are below that." Abu Hazra Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: from the garments of the people of Paradise, which no one knows." Abu al-'Aliya said: "Al-'abqari: velvet rugs, of a fineness beyond description." al-Qutaybi said: "Every embroidered cloth is called 'abqari among the Arabs." Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is attributed to a land where embroidery is made." al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: "Everything that is pleasing (nafis) among men and other things is called 'abqari among the Arabs." From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about 'Umar: "I have not seen a 'abqari making its ferry (fari) like him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3682), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2393), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

In any case, the description of the cushions of the people of the first two gardens is higher and more exalted than this description. For there He said: ﴿reclining on carpets whose linings are of brocade﴾. So He described the linings of their carpets and was silent about their outer surfaces, relying on what He praised in the linings, by way of priority and greater appropriateness. And the conclusion of the matter is that after the previously mentioned attributes He said: ﴿Is the reward of good (ihsan) anything but good?﴾ So He described its people with ihsan, which is the highest of ranks and ultimate ends, as in the hadith of Jibril when he asked about Islam and then about iman. These are numerous aspects of the superiority of the first two gardens over these latter two. We ask Allah, the Generous, the Giver, to make us among the people of the first two.

Then He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾, that is: He is worthy to be magnified so that He is not disobeyed, to be honoured so that He is worshipped, thanked so that He is not disbelieved in, and remembered so that He is not forgotten.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾: "Possessor of greatness and pride."

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban narrated to us, from 'Umayr ibn Hani', from Abu al-'Adhra', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be diligent (ajiddu) toward Allah, and He will forgive you."[[Al-Musnad (5/199). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Abu al-'Adhra', who is unknown (majhul)."]]

Also in another hadith: "Indeed, among the veneration of Allah is honouring the grey-haired Muslim, and the bearer of the Qur'an (in some copies: 'the dhikr') who is neither excessive in it nor neglectful of it, and the just ruler." (Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4843, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/163), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Yusuf al-Jizi (in the original and the rest of the copies: "al-Harbi"; the correction is from Abu Ya'la) narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording. (Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/445) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3522.)

Ibn Tahir said: "Rawh ibn Ubadah has also followed Mu'ammal in this, and Rawh is a trustworthy memorizer."
It was transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (3/396), via Rawh ibn Ubadah from Hammad ibn Salamah from...

Then (al-Tirmidhi) said: Mu'ammal erred in it; it is gharib (strange) and not mahfuz (preserved). Rather, this is narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan al-Maqdisi, from Rabi'ah ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording. (Musnad (4/177) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11563.)

Al-Jawhari said: "Alladha fulan bi-fulan" means: when he clung to him (persistently).

The saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour" means: keep to it (iltizam). It is also said: al-ilzaz is al-ilhah (insistence).

I say: both are close to each other, and Allah knows best; it means persistence, constancy, and insistence. In Sahih Muslim and the Four Sunan, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the salam, he would not sit except for as long as it takes to say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." (Sahih Muslim no. 592; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1512; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 298; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/69); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 924.)

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Rahman, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace].

These two gardens are below the previous two in rank, virtue, and standing, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾.

It has already been mentioned in a hadith: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them are of gold, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them are of silver. The first two are for those brought near (to Allah), and the latter two are for the companions of the right hand."[[In M: "فالأولتان" (the first two).]][[In M: "والأخيرتان" (the latter two).]]

Abu Musa said: "Two gardens of gold are for those brought near, and two gardens of silver are for the companions of the right hand."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾: "Besides them in degree." Ibn Zayd said: "Besides them in excellence."

The evidence for the superiority of the first two over the latter two is several-fold. First: He described the first two before these two, and placement first indicates special concern. Then He said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾. This clearly shows the superiority of what comes first and its elevation over the second.

Also, there He said: ﴿Both having branches﴾, that is, boughs or varieties of pleasures. Here He said: ﴿Dark green﴾, that is, deep green from the intensity of irrigation.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿Dark green﴾: "They have become black from the greenness, due to the intensity of irrigation with water."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Dark green﴾: he said, "Greenish-green." It is also narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, 'Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), 'Ata', 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafi', and Sufyan al-Thawri, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿Dark green﴾: "Full of greenness." Qatada said: "Greenish from irrigation, lush." There is no doubt about the freshness of the branches on trees that are interwoven with one another.

There He said: ﴿In both of them are two springs flowing﴾, and here He said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, "overflowing." Flowing is stronger than gushing.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾ means "full, never ceasing."

There He said: ﴿In both of them, of every fruit, two kinds﴾, and here He said: ﴿In both of them are fruit, and date palms and pomegranates﴾. There is no doubt that the first is more general and greater in number and variety, since "fruit" (fakiha) here is indefinite in an affirmative context and does not indicate all-inclusiveness. For this reason, His words ﴿and date palms and pomegranates﴾ are explained as the mention of a particular after a general, as al-Bukhari and others affirmed. The date palm and the pomegranate are singled out for mention only because of their nobility over other fruits.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Mukhariq narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates." They said: "Will they eat as they eat in this world?" He said: "Yes, and multiplied." They said: "Will they relieve themselves?" He said: "No, but they will perspire and exude, and Allah will remove whatever discomfort is in their bellies."[[Recorded in al-Muntakhab, no. 35, and in it is Husayn ibn 'Umar, who is abandoned (matruk).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The date palms of Paradise: their palm fronds are clothing for the people of Paradise, from which are their cut garments and their robes. Their spathes are red gold, their trunks are green emerald, their fruit is sweeter than honey and softer than butter, and it has no pit."

And my father narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salama, narrated to us, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I looked at Paradise, and a pomegranate from its pomegranates was like a saddled camel."[[Recorded by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, as cited in the takhrij of the Ihya' (6/2787), and by Ibn 'Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as cited in its abridgment (5/462), through the route of Abu Harun al-'Abdi. Abu Harun al-'Abdi, whose name is 'Umara ibn Juwayn, was declared a liar by some of the imams.]]

Then He said: ﴿In them are good, beautiful ones﴾. It was said: the meaning is many good things in Paradise, said by Qatada. It was also said: "good ones" is the plural of "khayyira," which is a righteous woman of good character and good appearance, said by the majority. It has been narrated with a elevated chain (marfu') from Umm Salama.[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/367) at length, and in it is Sulayman ibn Abi Karima, who is weak.]] In another hadith, which we will cite in the commentary on surah "al-Waqi'a" (on verses 35–38 of the same surah), the Hur al-'In sing: "We are the good, beautiful ones; we were created for noble husbands." For this reason, some read: "fihinna khayyarat," with shaddah (doubling), ﴿hisan﴾ (beautiful). ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾. There He said: ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾. There is no doubt that she who restrains her own gaze is more excellent than she who is made to restrain, even though all of them are veiled.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah who said: "For every Muslim there is a wife,[[The word "khayyira" is used here.]] and for every wife there is a tent, and for every tent there are four doors. Every day a gift, honor, and present that had not been before enters upon them: neither lively-mannered nor hot-tempered, neither bad-breathed nor foul-smelling, dark-eyed Hur, as if they were hidden eggs."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the pavilions﴾, al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tent of hollow pearl, its width is sixty miles, and in every corner of it are people whom the others do not see; the believers circulate among them."

He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and he said: "thirty miles."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4879) and (3243).]] Muslim also recorded it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and his wording is: "Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollow pearl, its length is sixty miles. The believer has people in it, and the believer circulates among them, but they do not see one another."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2838).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, Khulayd al-'Asri informed me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The tent is a single pearl, in which there are seventy doors of pearl."

And my father narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Abi Fatima narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾, and he said: "[In] pavilions of pearl, and in Paradise is one tent of a pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, upon it are four thousand gold doors."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and a dome of pearl, emerald, and ruby is set up for him, as wide as the distance between al-Jabiya and San'a'."

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2562), and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Rushdayn." Rushdayn was not alone in it, but Ibn Wahb followed him, as here, and in its chain is Darraj, who narrates strange reports (manakir) from Abu al-Haytham.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾: the same as previously stated, except that He added in describing the first ones the words ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?

* *

As for His words ﴿reclining on green cushions and beautiful rich carpets﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-rafraf: the cushions (al-mahabis)." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others: they are the mahabis. Al-'Ala' ibn Badr said: "Al-rafraf is over the couch, in the form of the hanging mahabis."

'Asim al-Jahdari said regarding ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: it means "the cushions." This is also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri in one narration from him.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: "The rafraf: the gardens of Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: "Al-'abqari: the zarabi (rugs/carpets)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the finest zarabi," meaning their best quality.

Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: brocade (dibaj)."

al-Hasan al-Basri was asked about His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾ and said: "They are the carpets of the people of Paradise—may you have no father—so seek them." It is also narrated from al-Hasan, in one report, that they are "the cushions (al-marafiq)." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-'abqari: red, yellow, and green." Al-'Ala' ibn Zayd was asked about al-'abqari and said: "The carpets are below that." Abu Hazra Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: from the garments of the people of Paradise, which no one knows." Abu al-'Aliya said: "Al-'abqari: velvet rugs, of a fineness beyond description." al-Qutaybi said: "Every embroidered cloth is called 'abqari among the Arabs." Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is attributed to a land where embroidery is made." al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: "Everything that is pleasing (nafis) among men and other things is called 'abqari among the Arabs." From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about 'Umar: "I have not seen a 'abqari making its ferry (fari) like him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3682), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2393), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

In any case, the description of the cushions of the people of the first two gardens is higher and more exalted than this description. For there He said: ﴿reclining on carpets whose linings are of brocade﴾. So He described the linings of their carpets and was silent about their outer surfaces, relying on what He praised in the linings, by way of priority and greater appropriateness. And the conclusion of the matter is that after the previously mentioned attributes He said: ﴿Is the reward of good (ihsan) anything but good?﴾ So He described its people with ihsan, which is the highest of ranks and ultimate ends, as in the hadith of Jibril when he asked about Islam and then about iman. These are numerous aspects of the superiority of the first two gardens over these latter two. We ask Allah, the Generous, the Giver, to make us among the people of the first two.

Then He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾, that is: He is worthy to be magnified so that He is not disobeyed, to be honoured so that He is worshipped, thanked so that He is not disbelieved in, and remembered so that He is not forgotten.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾: "Possessor of greatness and pride."

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban narrated to us, from 'Umayr ibn Hani', from Abu al-'Adhra', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be diligent (ajiddu) toward Allah, and He will forgive you."[[Al-Musnad (5/199). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Abu al-'Adhra', who is unknown (majhul)."]]

Also in another hadith: "Indeed, among the veneration of Allah is honouring the grey-haired Muslim, and the bearer of the Qur'an (in some copies: 'the dhikr') who is neither excessive in it nor neglectful of it, and the just ruler." (Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4843, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/163), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Yusuf al-Jizi (in the original and the rest of the copies: "al-Harbi"; the correction is from Abu Ya'la) narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording. (Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/445) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3522.)

Ibn Tahir said: "Rawh ibn Ubadah has also followed Mu'ammal in this, and Rawh is a trustworthy memorizer."
It was transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (3/396), via Rawh ibn Ubadah from Hammad ibn Salamah from...

Then (al-Tirmidhi) said: Mu'ammal erred in it; it is gharib (strange) and not mahfuz (preserved). Rather, this is narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan al-Maqdisi, from Rabi'ah ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording. (Musnad (4/177) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11563.)

Al-Jawhari said: "Alladha fulan bi-fulan" means: when he clung to him (persistently).

The saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour" means: keep to it (iltizam). It is also said: al-ilzaz is al-ilhah (insistence).

I say: both are close to each other, and Allah knows best; it means persistence, constancy, and insistence. In Sahih Muslim and the Four Sunan, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the salam, he would not sit except for as long as it takes to say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." (Sahih Muslim no. 592; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1512; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 298; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/69); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 924.)

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Rahman, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace].

These two gardens are below the previous two in rank, virtue, and standing, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾.

It has already been mentioned in a hadith: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them are of gold, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them are of silver. The first two are for those brought near (to Allah), and the latter two are for the companions of the right hand."[[In M: "فالأولتان" (the first two).]][[In M: "والأخيرتان" (the latter two).]]

Abu Musa said: "Two gardens of gold are for those brought near, and two gardens of silver are for the companions of the right hand."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾: "Besides them in degree." Ibn Zayd said: "Besides them in excellence."

The evidence for the superiority of the first two over the latter two is several-fold. First: He described the first two before these two, and placement first indicates special concern. Then He said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾. This clearly shows the superiority of what comes first and its elevation over the second.

Also, there He said: ﴿Both having branches﴾, that is, boughs or varieties of pleasures. Here He said: ﴿Dark green﴾, that is, deep green from the intensity of irrigation.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿Dark green﴾: "They have become black from the greenness, due to the intensity of irrigation with water."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Dark green﴾: he said, "Greenish-green." It is also narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, 'Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), 'Ata', 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafi', and Sufyan al-Thawri, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿Dark green﴾: "Full of greenness." Qatada said: "Greenish from irrigation, lush." There is no doubt about the freshness of the branches on trees that are interwoven with one another.

There He said: ﴿In both of them are two springs flowing﴾, and here He said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, "overflowing." Flowing is stronger than gushing.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾ means "full, never ceasing."

There He said: ﴿In both of them, of every fruit, two kinds﴾, and here He said: ﴿In both of them are fruit, and date palms and pomegranates﴾. There is no doubt that the first is more general and greater in number and variety, since "fruit" (fakiha) here is indefinite in an affirmative context and does not indicate all-inclusiveness. For this reason, His words ﴿and date palms and pomegranates﴾ are explained as the mention of a particular after a general, as al-Bukhari and others affirmed. The date palm and the pomegranate are singled out for mention only because of their nobility over other fruits.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Mukhariq narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates." They said: "Will they eat as they eat in this world?" He said: "Yes, and multiplied." They said: "Will they relieve themselves?" He said: "No, but they will perspire and exude, and Allah will remove whatever discomfort is in their bellies."[[Recorded in al-Muntakhab, no. 35, and in it is Husayn ibn 'Umar, who is abandoned (matruk).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The date palms of Paradise: their palm fronds are clothing for the people of Paradise, from which are their cut garments and their robes. Their spathes are red gold, their trunks are green emerald, their fruit is sweeter than honey and softer than butter, and it has no pit."

And my father narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salama, narrated to us, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I looked at Paradise, and a pomegranate from its pomegranates was like a saddled camel."[[Recorded by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, as cited in the takhrij of the Ihya' (6/2787), and by Ibn 'Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as cited in its abridgment (5/462), through the route of Abu Harun al-'Abdi. Abu Harun al-'Abdi, whose name is 'Umara ibn Juwayn, was declared a liar by some of the imams.]]

Then He said: ﴿In them are good, beautiful ones﴾. It was said: the meaning is many good things in Paradise, said by Qatada. It was also said: "good ones" is the plural of "khayyira," which is a righteous woman of good character and good appearance, said by the majority. It has been narrated with a elevated chain (marfu') from Umm Salama.[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/367) at length, and in it is Sulayman ibn Abi Karima, who is weak.]] In another hadith, which we will cite in the commentary on surah "al-Waqi'a" (on verses 35–38 of the same surah), the Hur al-'In sing: "We are the good, beautiful ones; we were created for noble husbands." For this reason, some read: "fihinna khayyarat," with shaddah (doubling), ﴿hisan﴾ (beautiful). ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾. There He said: ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾. There is no doubt that she who restrains her own gaze is more excellent than she who is made to restrain, even though all of them are veiled.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah who said: "For every Muslim there is a wife,[[The word "khayyira" is used here.]] and for every wife there is a tent, and for every tent there are four doors. Every day a gift, honor, and present that had not been before enters upon them: neither lively-mannered nor hot-tempered, neither bad-breathed nor foul-smelling, dark-eyed Hur, as if they were hidden eggs."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the pavilions﴾, al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tent of hollow pearl, its width is sixty miles, and in every corner of it are people whom the others do not see; the believers circulate among them."

He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and he said: "thirty miles."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4879) and (3243).]] Muslim also recorded it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and his wording is: "Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollow pearl, its length is sixty miles. The believer has people in it, and the believer circulates among them, but they do not see one another."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2838).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, Khulayd al-'Asri informed me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The tent is a single pearl, in which there are seventy doors of pearl."

And my father narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Abi Fatima narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾, and he said: "[In] pavilions of pearl, and in Paradise is one tent of a pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, upon it are four thousand gold doors."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and a dome of pearl, emerald, and ruby is set up for him, as wide as the distance between al-Jabiya and San'a'."

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2562), and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Rushdayn." Rushdayn was not alone in it, but Ibn Wahb followed him, as here, and in its chain is Darraj, who narrates strange reports (manakir) from Abu al-Haytham.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾: the same as previously stated, except that He added in describing the first ones the words ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?

* *

As for His words ﴿reclining on green cushions and beautiful rich carpets﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-rafraf: the cushions (al-mahabis)." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others: they are the mahabis. Al-'Ala' ibn Badr said: "Al-rafraf is over the couch, in the form of the hanging mahabis."

'Asim al-Jahdari said regarding ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: it means "the cushions." This is also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri in one narration from him.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: "The rafraf: the gardens of Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: "Al-'abqari: the zarabi (rugs/carpets)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the finest zarabi," meaning their best quality.

Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: brocade (dibaj)."

al-Hasan al-Basri was asked about His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾ and said: "They are the carpets of the people of Paradise—may you have no father—so seek them." It is also narrated from al-Hasan, in one report, that they are "the cushions (al-marafiq)." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-'abqari: red, yellow, and green." Al-'Ala' ibn Zayd was asked about al-'abqari and said: "The carpets are below that." Abu Hazra Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: from the garments of the people of Paradise, which no one knows." Abu al-'Aliya said: "Al-'abqari: velvet rugs, of a fineness beyond description." al-Qutaybi said: "Every embroidered cloth is called 'abqari among the Arabs." Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is attributed to a land where embroidery is made." al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: "Everything that is pleasing (nafis) among men and other things is called 'abqari among the Arabs." From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about 'Umar: "I have not seen a 'abqari making its ferry (fari) like him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3682), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2393), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

In any case, the description of the cushions of the people of the first two gardens is higher and more exalted than this description. For there He said: ﴿reclining on carpets whose linings are of brocade﴾. So He described the linings of their carpets and was silent about their outer surfaces, relying on what He praised in the linings, by way of priority and greater appropriateness. And the conclusion of the matter is that after the previously mentioned attributes He said: ﴿Is the reward of good (ihsan) anything but good?﴾ So He described its people with ihsan, which is the highest of ranks and ultimate ends, as in the hadith of Jibril when he asked about Islam and then about iman. These are numerous aspects of the superiority of the first two gardens over these latter two. We ask Allah, the Generous, the Giver, to make us among the people of the first two.

Then He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾, that is: He is worthy to be magnified so that He is not disobeyed, to be honoured so that He is worshipped, thanked so that He is not disbelieved in, and remembered so that He is not forgotten.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾: "Possessor of greatness and pride."

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban narrated to us, from 'Umayr ibn Hani', from Abu al-'Adhra', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be diligent (ajiddu) toward Allah, and He will forgive you."[[Al-Musnad (5/199). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Abu al-'Adhra', who is unknown (majhul)."]]

Also in another hadith: "Indeed, among the veneration of Allah is honouring the grey-haired Muslim, and the bearer of the Qur'an (in some copies: 'the dhikr') who is neither excessive in it nor neglectful of it, and the just ruler." (Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4843, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/163), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Yusuf al-Jizi (in the original and the rest of the copies: "al-Harbi"; the correction is from Abu Ya'la) narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording. (Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/445) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3522.)

Ibn Tahir said: "Rawh ibn Ubadah has also followed Mu'ammal in this, and Rawh is a trustworthy memorizer."
It was transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (3/396), via Rawh ibn Ubadah from Hammad ibn Salamah from...

Then (al-Tirmidhi) said: Mu'ammal erred in it; it is gharib (strange) and not mahfuz (preserved). Rather, this is narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan al-Maqdisi, from Rabi'ah ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording. (Musnad (4/177) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11563.)

Al-Jawhari said: "Alladha fulan bi-fulan" means: when he clung to him (persistently).

The saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour" means: keep to it (iltizam). It is also said: al-ilzaz is al-ilhah (insistence).

I say: both are close to each other, and Allah knows best; it means persistence, constancy, and insistence. In Sahih Muslim and the Four Sunan, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the salam, he would not sit except for as long as it takes to say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." (Sahih Muslim no. 592; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1512; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 298; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/69); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 924.)

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Rahman, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace].

These two gardens are below the previous two in rank, virtue, and standing, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾.

It has already been mentioned in a hadith: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them are of gold, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them are of silver. The first two are for those brought near (to Allah), and the latter two are for the companions of the right hand."[[In M: "فالأولتان" (the first two).]][[In M: "والأخيرتان" (the latter two).]]

Abu Musa said: "Two gardens of gold are for those brought near, and two gardens of silver are for the companions of the right hand."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾: "Besides them in degree." Ibn Zayd said: "Besides them in excellence."

The evidence for the superiority of the first two over the latter two is several-fold. First: He described the first two before these two, and placement first indicates special concern. Then He said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾. This clearly shows the superiority of what comes first and its elevation over the second.

Also, there He said: ﴿Both having branches﴾, that is, boughs or varieties of pleasures. Here He said: ﴿Dark green﴾, that is, deep green from the intensity of irrigation.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿Dark green﴾: "They have become black from the greenness, due to the intensity of irrigation with water."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Dark green﴾: he said, "Greenish-green." It is also narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, 'Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), 'Ata', 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafi', and Sufyan al-Thawri, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿Dark green﴾: "Full of greenness." Qatada said: "Greenish from irrigation, lush." There is no doubt about the freshness of the branches on trees that are interwoven with one another.

There He said: ﴿In both of them are two springs flowing﴾, and here He said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, "overflowing." Flowing is stronger than gushing.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾ means "full, never ceasing."

There He said: ﴿In both of them, of every fruit, two kinds﴾, and here He said: ﴿In both of them are fruit, and date palms and pomegranates﴾. There is no doubt that the first is more general and greater in number and variety, since "fruit" (fakiha) here is indefinite in an affirmative context and does not indicate all-inclusiveness. For this reason, His words ﴿and date palms and pomegranates﴾ are explained as the mention of a particular after a general, as al-Bukhari and others affirmed. The date palm and the pomegranate are singled out for mention only because of their nobility over other fruits.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Mukhariq narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates." They said: "Will they eat as they eat in this world?" He said: "Yes, and multiplied." They said: "Will they relieve themselves?" He said: "No, but they will perspire and exude, and Allah will remove whatever discomfort is in their bellies."[[Recorded in al-Muntakhab, no. 35, and in it is Husayn ibn 'Umar, who is abandoned (matruk).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The date palms of Paradise: their palm fronds are clothing for the people of Paradise, from which are their cut garments and their robes. Their spathes are red gold, their trunks are green emerald, their fruit is sweeter than honey and softer than butter, and it has no pit."

And my father narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salama, narrated to us, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I looked at Paradise, and a pomegranate from its pomegranates was like a saddled camel."[[Recorded by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, as cited in the takhrij of the Ihya' (6/2787), and by Ibn 'Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as cited in its abridgment (5/462), through the route of Abu Harun al-'Abdi. Abu Harun al-'Abdi, whose name is 'Umara ibn Juwayn, was declared a liar by some of the imams.]]

Then He said: ﴿In them are good, beautiful ones﴾. It was said: the meaning is many good things in Paradise, said by Qatada. It was also said: "good ones" is the plural of "khayyira," which is a righteous woman of good character and good appearance, said by the majority. It has been narrated with a elevated chain (marfu') from Umm Salama.[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/367) at length, and in it is Sulayman ibn Abi Karima, who is weak.]] In another hadith, which we will cite in the commentary on surah "al-Waqi'a" (on verses 35–38 of the same surah), the Hur al-'In sing: "We are the good, beautiful ones; we were created for noble husbands." For this reason, some read: "fihinna khayyarat," with shaddah (doubling), ﴿hisan﴾ (beautiful). ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾. There He said: ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾. There is no doubt that she who restrains her own gaze is more excellent than she who is made to restrain, even though all of them are veiled.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah who said: "For every Muslim there is a wife,[[The word "khayyira" is used here.]] and for every wife there is a tent, and for every tent there are four doors. Every day a gift, honor, and present that had not been before enters upon them: neither lively-mannered nor hot-tempered, neither bad-breathed nor foul-smelling, dark-eyed Hur, as if they were hidden eggs."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the pavilions﴾, al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tent of hollow pearl, its width is sixty miles, and in every corner of it are people whom the others do not see; the believers circulate among them."

He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and he said: "thirty miles."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4879) and (3243).]] Muslim also recorded it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and his wording is: "Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollow pearl, its length is sixty miles. The believer has people in it, and the believer circulates among them, but they do not see one another."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2838).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, Khulayd al-'Asri informed me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The tent is a single pearl, in which there are seventy doors of pearl."

And my father narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Abi Fatima narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾, and he said: "[In] pavilions of pearl, and in Paradise is one tent of a pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, upon it are four thousand gold doors."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and a dome of pearl, emerald, and ruby is set up for him, as wide as the distance between al-Jabiya and San'a'."

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2562), and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Rushdayn." Rushdayn was not alone in it, but Ibn Wahb followed him, as here, and in its chain is Darraj, who narrates strange reports (manakir) from Abu al-Haytham.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾: the same as previously stated, except that He added in describing the first ones the words ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?

* *

As for His words ﴿reclining on green cushions and beautiful rich carpets﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-rafraf: the cushions (al-mahabis)." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others: they are the mahabis. Al-'Ala' ibn Badr said: "Al-rafraf is over the couch, in the form of the hanging mahabis."

'Asim al-Jahdari said regarding ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: it means "the cushions." This is also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri in one narration from him.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: "The rafraf: the gardens of Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: "Al-'abqari: the zarabi (rugs/carpets)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the finest zarabi," meaning their best quality.

Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: brocade (dibaj)."

al-Hasan al-Basri was asked about His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾ and said: "They are the carpets of the people of Paradise—may you have no father—so seek them." It is also narrated from al-Hasan, in one report, that they are "the cushions (al-marafiq)." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-'abqari: red, yellow, and green." Al-'Ala' ibn Zayd was asked about al-'abqari and said: "The carpets are below that." Abu Hazra Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: from the garments of the people of Paradise, which no one knows." Abu al-'Aliya said: "Al-'abqari: velvet rugs, of a fineness beyond description." al-Qutaybi said: "Every embroidered cloth is called 'abqari among the Arabs." Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is attributed to a land where embroidery is made." al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: "Everything that is pleasing (nafis) among men and other things is called 'abqari among the Arabs." From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about 'Umar: "I have not seen a 'abqari making its ferry (fari) like him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3682), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2393), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

In any case, the description of the cushions of the people of the first two gardens is higher and more exalted than this description. For there He said: ﴿reclining on carpets whose linings are of brocade﴾. So He described the linings of their carpets and was silent about their outer surfaces, relying on what He praised in the linings, by way of priority and greater appropriateness. And the conclusion of the matter is that after the previously mentioned attributes He said: ﴿Is the reward of good (ihsan) anything but good?﴾ So He described its people with ihsan, which is the highest of ranks and ultimate ends, as in the hadith of Jibril when he asked about Islam and then about iman. These are numerous aspects of the superiority of the first two gardens over these latter two. We ask Allah, the Generous, the Giver, to make us among the people of the first two.

Then He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾, that is: He is worthy to be magnified so that He is not disobeyed, to be honoured so that He is worshipped, thanked so that He is not disbelieved in, and remembered so that He is not forgotten.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾: "Possessor of greatness and pride."

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban narrated to us, from 'Umayr ibn Hani', from Abu al-'Adhra', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be diligent (ajiddu) toward Allah, and He will forgive you."[[Al-Musnad (5/199). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Abu al-'Adhra', who is unknown (majhul)."]]

Also in another hadith: "Indeed, among the veneration of Allah is honouring the grey-haired Muslim, and the bearer of the Qur'an (in some copies: 'the dhikr') who is neither excessive in it nor neglectful of it, and the just ruler." (Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4843, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/163), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Yusuf al-Jizi (in the original and the rest of the copies: "al-Harbi"; the correction is from Abu Ya'la) narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording. (Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/445) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3522.)

Ibn Tahir said: "Rawh ibn Ubadah has also followed Mu'ammal in this, and Rawh is a trustworthy memorizer."
It was transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (3/396), via Rawh ibn Ubadah from Hammad ibn Salamah from...

Then (al-Tirmidhi) said: Mu'ammal erred in it; it is gharib (strange) and not mahfuz (preserved). Rather, this is narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan al-Maqdisi, from Rabi'ah ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording. (Musnad (4/177) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11563.)

Al-Jawhari said: "Alladha fulan bi-fulan" means: when he clung to him (persistently).

The saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour" means: keep to it (iltizam). It is also said: al-ilzaz is al-ilhah (insistence).

I say: both are close to each other, and Allah knows best; it means persistence, constancy, and insistence. In Sahih Muslim and the Four Sunan, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the salam, he would not sit except for as long as it takes to say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." (Sahih Muslim no. 592; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1512; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 298; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/69); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 924.)

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Rahman, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace].

These two gardens are below the previous two in rank, virtue, and standing, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾.

It has already been mentioned in a hadith: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them are of gold, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them are of silver. The first two are for those brought near (to Allah), and the latter two are for the companions of the right hand."[[In M: "فالأولتان" (the first two).]][[In M: "والأخيرتان" (the latter two).]]

Abu Musa said: "Two gardens of gold are for those brought near, and two gardens of silver are for the companions of the right hand."

Ibn 'Abbas said regarding ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾: "Besides them in degree." Ibn Zayd said: "Besides them in excellence."

The evidence for the superiority of the first two over the latter two is several-fold. First: He described the first two before these two, and placement first indicates special concern. Then He said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾. This clearly shows the superiority of what comes first and its elevation over the second.

Also, there He said: ﴿Both having branches﴾, that is, boughs or varieties of pleasures. Here He said: ﴿Dark green﴾, that is, deep green from the intensity of irrigation.

Ibn 'Abbas said concerning His words ﴿Dark green﴾: "They have become black from the greenness, due to the intensity of irrigation with water."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿Dark green﴾: he said, "Greenish-green." It is also narrated from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, 'Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa, 'Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid (in one of the narrations), 'Ata', 'Atiyya al-'Awfi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Yahya ibn Rafi', and Sufyan al-Thawri, something similar.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: ﴿Dark green﴾: "Full of greenness." Qatada said: "Greenish from irrigation, lush." There is no doubt about the freshness of the branches on trees that are interwoven with one another.

There He said: ﴿In both of them are two springs flowing﴾, and here He said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, "overflowing." Flowing is stronger than gushing.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Two gushing springs﴾ means "full, never ceasing."

There He said: ﴿In both of them, of every fruit, two kinds﴾, and here He said: ﴿In both of them are fruit, and date palms and pomegranates﴾. There is no doubt that the first is more general and greater in number and variety, since "fruit" (fakiha) here is indefinite in an affirmative context and does not indicate all-inclusiveness. For this reason, His words ﴿and date palms and pomegranates﴾ are explained as the mention of a particular after a general, as al-Bukhari and others affirmed. The date palm and the pomegranate are singled out for mention only because of their nobility over other fruits.

'Abd ibn Humayd said: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, Husayn ibn 'Umar narrated to us, Mukhariq narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Shihab, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, is there fruit in Paradise?" He said: "Yes, there is fruit, date palms and pomegranates." They said: "Will they eat as they eat in this world?" He said: "Yes, and multiplied." They said: "Will they relieve themselves?" He said: "No, but they will perspire and exude, and Allah will remove whatever discomfort is in their bellies."[[Recorded in al-Muntakhab, no. 35, and in it is Husayn ibn 'Umar, who is abandoned (matruk).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Fadl ibn Dukayn narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "The date palms of Paradise: their palm fronds are clothing for the people of Paradise, from which are their cut garments and their robes. Their spathes are red gold, their trunks are green emerald, their fruit is sweeter than honey and softer than butter, and it has no pit."

And my father narrated to us: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salama, narrated to us, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I looked at Paradise, and a pomegranate from its pomegranates was like a saddled camel."[[Recorded by al-Tha'labi in his tafsir, as cited in the takhrij of the Ihya' (6/2787), and by Ibn 'Asakir in Tarikh Dimashq, as cited in its abridgment (5/462), through the route of Abu Harun al-'Abdi. Abu Harun al-'Abdi, whose name is 'Umara ibn Juwayn, was declared a liar by some of the imams.]]

Then He said: ﴿In them are good, beautiful ones﴾. It was said: the meaning is many good things in Paradise, said by Qatada. It was also said: "good ones" is the plural of "khayyira," which is a righteous woman of good character and good appearance, said by the majority. It has been narrated with a elevated chain (marfu') from Umm Salama.[[Recorded by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (23/367) at length, and in it is Sulayman ibn Abi Karima, who is weak.]] In another hadith, which we will cite in the commentary on surah "al-Waqi'a" (on verses 35–38 of the same surah), the Hur al-'In sing: "We are the good, beautiful ones; we were created for noble husbands." For this reason, some read: "fihinna khayyarat," with shaddah (doubling), ﴿hisan﴾ (beautiful). ﴿So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?﴾

Then He said: ﴿Fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾. There He said: ﴿In them are those restraining their gaze﴾. There is no doubt that she who restrains her own gaze is more excellent than she who is made to restrain, even though all of them are veiled.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Awdi narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Abu 'Ubayda, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah who said: "For every Muslim there is a wife,[[The word "khayyira" is used here.]] and for every wife there is a tent, and for every tent there are four doors. Every day a gift, honor, and present that had not been before enters upon them: neither lively-mannered nor hot-tempered, neither bad-breathed nor foul-smelling, dark-eyed Hur, as if they were hidden eggs."

* *

As for His words ﴿in the pavilions﴾, al-Bukhari said:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Qays, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tent of hollow pearl, its width is sixty miles, and in every corner of it are people whom the others do not see; the believers circulate among them."

He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and he said: "thirty miles."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4879) and (3243).]] Muslim also recorded it from the hadith of Abu 'Imran, with the same chain, and his wording is: "Indeed, for the believer in Paradise there is a tent of a single hollow pearl, its length is sixty miles. The believer has people in it, and the believer circulates among them, but they do not see one another."[[Sahih Muslim, no. (2838).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Rabi' narrated to us, 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, Khulayd al-'Asri informed me, from Abu al-Darda', who said: "The tent is a single pearl, in which there are seventy doors of pearl."

And my father narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Abi Fatima narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words ﴿fair ones, restrained in pavilions﴾, and he said: "[In] pavilions of pearl, and in Paradise is one tent of a pearl, four farsakhs by four farsakhs, upon it are four thousand gold doors."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: 'Amr informed us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is the one who has eighty thousand servants and seventy-two wives, and a dome of pearl, emerald, and ruby is set up for him, as wide as the distance between al-Jabiya and San'a'."

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from the hadith of 'Amr ibn al-Harith, with the same chain.[[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2562), and he said: "This is a gharib hadith; we only know it from the hadith of Rushdayn." Rushdayn was not alone in it, but Ibn Wahb followed him, as here, and in its chain is Darraj, who narrates strange reports (manakir) from Abu al-Haytham.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿Neither man nor jinn has touched them before them﴾: the same as previously stated, except that He added in describing the first ones the words ﴿as if they were rubies and coral﴾. So which of the favours of your Lord would you deny?

* *

As for His words ﴿reclining on green cushions and beautiful rich carpets﴾: 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Al-rafraf: the cushions (al-mahabis)." Likewise said Mujahid, 'Ikrima, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and others: they are the mahabis. Al-'Ala' ibn Badr said: "Al-rafraf is over the couch, in the form of the hanging mahabis."

'Asim al-Jahdari said regarding ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: it means "the cushions." This is also the view of al-Hasan al-Basri in one narration from him.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿reclining on green rafraf﴾: "The rafraf: the gardens of Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi said: "Al-'abqari: the zarabi (rugs/carpets)." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "They are the finest zarabi," meaning their best quality.

Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: brocade (dibaj)."

al-Hasan al-Basri was asked about His words ﴿and beautiful rich carpets﴾ and said: "They are the carpets of the people of Paradise—may you have no father—so seek them." It is also narrated from al-Hasan, in one report, that they are "the cushions (al-marafiq)." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "Al-'abqari: red, yellow, and green." Al-'Ala' ibn Zayd was asked about al-'abqari and said: "The carpets are below that." Abu Hazra Ya'qub ibn Mujahid said: "Al-'abqari: from the garments of the people of Paradise, which no one knows." Abu al-'Aliya said: "Al-'abqari: velvet rugs, of a fineness beyond description." al-Qutaybi said: "Every embroidered cloth is called 'abqari among the Arabs." Abu 'Ubayda said: "It is attributed to a land where embroidery is made." al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: "Everything that is pleasing (nafis) among men and other things is called 'abqari among the Arabs." From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ about 'Umar: "I have not seen a 'abqari making its ferry (fari) like him."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (3682), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2393), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

In any case, the description of the cushions of the people of the first two gardens is higher and more exalted than this description. For there He said: ﴿reclining on carpets whose linings are of brocade﴾. So He described the linings of their carpets and was silent about their outer surfaces, relying on what He praised in the linings, by way of priority and greater appropriateness. And the conclusion of the matter is that after the previously mentioned attributes He said: ﴿Is the reward of good (ihsan) anything but good?﴾ So He described its people with ihsan, which is the highest of ranks and ultimate ends, as in the hadith of Jibril when he asked about Islam and then about iman. These are numerous aspects of the superiority of the first two gardens over these latter two. We ask Allah, the Generous, the Giver, to make us among the people of the first two.

Then He said: ﴿Blessed is the name of your Lord, Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾, that is: He is worthy to be magnified so that He is not disobeyed, to be honoured so that He is worshipped, thanked so that He is not disbelieved in, and remembered so that He is not forgotten.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿Possessor of Majesty and Honour﴾: "Possessor of greatness and pride."

Imam Ahmad said: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban narrated to us, from 'Umayr ibn Hani', from Abu al-'Adhra', from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Be diligent (ajiddu) toward Allah, and He will forgive you."[[Al-Musnad (5/199). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Abu al-'Adhra', who is unknown (majhul)."]]

Also in another hadith: "Indeed, among the veneration of Allah is honouring the grey-haired Muslim, and the bearer of the Qur'an (in some copies: 'the dhikr') who is neither excessive in it nor neglectful of it, and the just ruler." (Narrated by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. 4843, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8/163), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.)

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Yusuf al-Jizi (in the original and the rest of the copies: "al-Harbi"; the correction is from Abu Ya'la) narrated to us, Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Similarly, al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il, from Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same wording. (Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/445) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3522.)

Ibn Tahir said: "Rawh ibn Ubadah has also followed Mu'ammal in this, and Rawh is a trustworthy memorizer."
It was transmitted by Ibn Mardawayh in his Tafsir, as cited in Takhrij al-Kashshaf by al-Zayla'i (3/396), via Rawh ibn Ubadah from Hammad ibn Salamah from...

Then (al-Tirmidhi) said: Mu'ammal erred in it; it is gharib (strange) and not mahfuz (preserved). Rather, this is narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Imam Ahmad said: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Hassan al-Maqdisi, from Rabi'ah ibn 'Amir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording. (Musnad (4/177) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 11563.)

Al-Jawhari said: "Alladha fulan bi-fulan" means: when he clung to him (persistently).

The saying of Ibn Mas'ud: "Persist in saying: O Possessor of Majesty and Honour" means: keep to it (iltizam). It is also said: al-ilzaz is al-ilhah (insistence).

I say: both are close to each other, and Allah knows best; it means persistence, constancy, and insistence. In Sahih Muslim and the Four Sunan, from the hadith of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from Aishah, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished the salam, he would not sit except for as long as it takes to say: "O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace; blessed are You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honour." (Sahih Muslim no. 592; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 1512; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 298; Sunan al-Nasa'i (3/69); Sunan Ibn Majah no. 924.)

End of the tafsir of Surah al-Rahman, and to Allah belongs all praise [and grace].

These two gardens are below the previous two in rank, virtue, and standing, according to the explicit text of the Qur'an. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And besides these two, there are two other gardens﴾.

It has already been mentioned in a hadith: "Two gardens of gold, their vessels and everything in them are of gold, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and everything in them are of silver.
